dialectical-transformation-is-fully-reli.text: The irreversible premise-to-justified transformation during challenge is both semantics-preserving (the resulting node inherits complete outlist evaluation with conjunction, absence, and persistence semantics) and crash-safe (recursive dialectical chains terminate deterministically), making dialectical operations reliable despite their irreversibility.

justifications.label: Irreversibility is safe because both semantic inheritance and operational termination are guaranteed

dialectical-transformation-is-operationa.text: The irreversible premise-to-justified transformation during challenge is both semantically safe (inherits uniform outlist evaluation and truth maintenance properties from the dialectical structure) and operationally safe (executes within atomic load/save transactions with deterministic BFS propagation).

justifications.label: depth-4 — challenge is the most destructive semantic operation (it permanently changes node identity) so proving it is operationally atomic AND semantically preserving is a meaningful safety property

dialectical-transformation-preserves-sem.text: Challenging a premise irreversibly transforms its identity from unjustified to justified node, but the resulting dialectical structure inherits complete outlist semantics — conjunction over multiple outlists, absence-as-OUT permissiveness, and persistence survival — ensuring the transformation preserves well-defined evaluable behavior.

justifications.label: depth-3 — the identity transformation (premise → justified) is destructive, but the semantic framework (outlist rules) remains intact across the transformation

dialectics-achieve-forward-reliability-a.text: Dialectical operations achieve complete bidirectional assurance: forward activation is deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete (challenge/defend evaluated uniformly with controlled irreversibility), while backward reversal is topology-complete with surgical guided recovery (recovery reaches all transitively dependent nodes, hints target only cascade victims with surviving premises) — the full dialectical cycle from engagement through resolution is assured in both directions.

justifications.label: dialectical operations assured both in forward engagement and backward recovery

dialectics-are-atomic-and-transparent.text: Challenge/defend dialectics are both semantically transparent (indistinguishable from ordinary beliefs, evaluated by uniform outlist rules) and atomically safe (mutations follow the same context-managed load/save pipeline as all other operations), requiring no special transaction handling.

justifications.label: depth-4 — dialectics inherit both semantic uniformity and mutation safety from the shared infrastructure

dialectics-are-deterministic-and-reliabl.text: Dialectical challenge/defend operations are simultaneously deterministic (through semantic transparency inheriting uniform evaluation rules from the core TMS) and fully reliable (semantics-preserving with crash safety through terminating propagation) — achieving safe predictable behavior without dedicated dialectical machinery.

justifications.label: Deterministic dialectics (via transparency) + reliable dialectics (via crash-safe propagation) → dialectics are both predictable and dependable

dialectics-are-deterministic-by-transpar.text: Dialectical challenge/defend structures receive deterministic reversible evaluation without special-casing — semantic transparency ensures the deterministic engine treats dialectical nodes identically to ordinary beliefs, so dialectical correctness requires no independent proof.

justifications.label: transparent nodes evaluated by deterministic engine without distinction (depth-4 from two depth-3 IN)

dialectics-are-dually-grounded-by-purity.text: Dialectical operations achieve dual semantic grounding from independent sources: evaluation purity (uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free validity checking) enables richly-governed exception-safe dialectics, while uniform edge-case semantics transitively ground deterministic reliable dialectics through complete negative semantics — together ensuring dialectics are both governable and semantically well-founded from first principles.

justifications.label: dialectics grounded independently by evaluation purity and semantic uniformity

dialectics-are-semantically-transparent.text: Challenge/defend dialectics are semantically indistinguishable from ordinary beliefs: they inherit fully-specified outlist semantics (conjunction, absence-as-OUT, persistence) and are evaluated by the same uniform pure rules that govern all truth maintenance — no dialectical special cases exist anywhere in the engine.

justifications.label: Complete outlist semantics (depth-2) + uniform truth evaluation (depth-2) together prove dialectical nodes have no privileged or special-case behavior

dialectics-complete-the-revision-system.text: The system handles both automated belief revision (outlist defeat for proactive retraction, dependency-directed backtracking for reactive contradiction resolution) and interactive dialectics (challenge/defend for human-driven contestation) — both operating atomically through the same outlist primitive with transparent, uniform evaluation semantics.

justifications.label: Automated revision handles machine-detected contradictions; dialectics handle human-initiated contestation — together they span the full space of belief challenges

dialectics-inherit-complete-outlist-sema.text: The recursive challenge/defend dialectical system inherits fully-specified semantics from the outlist primitive: conjunction over multiple outlists, absent-means-OUT permissiveness, and persistence guarantees all apply to dialectical structures without additional rules.

justifications.label: Dialectical structure is pure outlist, so all outlist semantic guarantees transfer directly

direct-access-raises-list-access-filters.text: API functions for single-node access (`show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`) raise `PermissionError` on forbidden nodes, while list/export functions (`list_nodes`, `search`, `export_network`) silently exclude them from results.

dispute-resolution-is-complete-and-relia.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms — intentional (dialectical challenge/defend with irreversible premise transformation) and automated (contradiction detection with dependency-directed backtracking) — are individually fully reliable, crash-safe, and traceable, leaving no dispute pathway that could silently fail or lose history.

justifications.label: Dialectical reliability (depth-4) and contradiction traceability (depth-4) are independently established; together they show the system resolves disputes at every level without silent failure

dispute-resolution-is-topology-accurate.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms — intentional dialectical challenge/defend and automated contradiction resolution — propagate their effects through an accurate convergent topology with complete dependency tracking, ensuring every transitively affected node reaches its correct truth state after any dispute.

justifications.label: Complete dispute resolution (depth-5) operating on accurate topology (depth-7) guarantees disputes resolve across the true dependency graph — no affected node is silently left in an inconsistent state

dispute-resolution-spans-all-origins.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms (intentional dialectical and automated contradiction) are complete and reliable, and all belief origins participate in the same deterministic revision pipeline — every belief from any source can be disputed and resolved through identical mechanisms.

justifications.label: complete dispute resolution plus origin-agnostic deterministic revision ensures all beliefs are uniformly disputable

domain-data-must-be-reconstructed-via-im.text: The belief graph (`network.json`), exported beliefs (`beliefs.md`), and individual entry files (`entries/`) are excluded from version control and must be reconstructed through import pipelines (`import_beliefs`, `import_agent`) rather than read from the repository.

double-roundtrip-is-idempotent.text: `export_markdown(import_into_network(export_markdown(net)))` must produce markdown identical to `export_markdown(net)`, with the sole permitted difference being `updated_at` timestamp lines that change per import.

dry-run-prevents-both-retraction-and-met.text: The `dry_run` flag in review-beliefs prevents both truth-value changes (retraction of invalid beliefs) and metadata side-effects (`last_reviewed` timestamp, `review_result` classification), making it fully read-only — extending beyond what `auto-retract-respects-dry-run` covers.

dual-backend-atomicity-is-feature-comple.text: Both storage backends provide atomic isolated operations with complete API coverage — the SQLite backend's context-managed mutations and PgApi's per-method transactions cover the same full set of operations

justifications.label: Backend-independent atomicity achieves full feature parity only when PgApi implements the complete API surface

dual-mode-makes-exactly-three-llm-calls.text: Dual mode performs exactly three `invoke_model` calls in sequence: TMS-leg answer → FTS-leg answer → merged synthesis answer.

dual-mode-requires-sources-db.text: `ask()` with `dual=True` raises `ValueError` immediately if `sources_db` is `None`, since the dual retrieval path (TMS + FTS-RAG merge) is meaningless without a source-chunk database.

dual-package-distribution-split.text: `reasons/` and `reasons_lib/` form a full-versus-library distribution split: `reasons` adds merkle proofs and metadata on top of the shared TMS core modules, while `reasons_lib` ships the lighter variant without those additions.

dual-package-layout-reasons-and-reasons-.text: The repo maintains two import trees (`reasons/` and `reasons_lib/`) with identical module names; tests import from `reasons`, and `pyproject.toml` may alias one to the other, so a developer must verify which tree is canonical before editing.

dual-quality-enforcement-spans-automated.text: Belief quality is enforced by two independent mechanisms that cannot interfere: automated self-correction autonomously maintains consistency through contradiction resolution and staleness detection, while explicit quality review independently evaluates derived beliefs with read-only fault tolerance — dual enforcement ensures quality even when one mechanism is insufficient.

justifications.label: Automated self-correction and read-only review provide independent non-interfering quality enforcement

dual-quality-gates-are-complementary-and.text: The system enforces belief quality through dual non-mutating gates targeting complementary validity dimensions: review validates logical soundness of derived beliefs (scoped to justified nodes, dry-run gated auto-retraction), while staleness checking validates source currency of all IN beliefs (conservative CI gate with nonzero exit on drift) — neither gate can corrupt network state.

justifications.label: Review validates logical soundness while staleness validates source currency

dual-storage-backends-are-interchangeabl.text: Both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends can be used interchangeably for any operation, with identical safety guarantees through backend-appropriate mechanisms and complete API surface coverage, so applications can switch backends without behavioral changes.

justifications.label: Backend safety equivalence (depth-4) and backend-independent atomicity (depth-2) establish interchangeability, but only when PgApi achieves full API coverage — partial coverage means some operations work on SQLite but not PostgreSQL

duplicate-node-id-raises-valueerror.text: `api.add_node()` raises `ValueError` when given a node ID that already exists in the network — node IDs are unique.

each-cli-test-creates-isolated-db.text: Every CLI test method initializes a fresh SQLite database via `run_cli("init")` in a pytest `tmp_path`, ensuring zero shared state between tests.

edge-case-safety-spans-creation-and-main.text: The system handles edge cases safely across both temporal dimensions: at creation time, uniform revision covers all semantic edge cases (vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents) through minimal primitives; at maintenance time, contradiction resolution and staleness detection actively catch drift — no edge case is safe only at one point in time.

justifications.label: Edge-case uniformity at creation (depth-5) combined with bidirectional self-correction at maintenance (depth-4) closes the temporal gap where edge cases could escape handling

edge-case-uniformity-follows-from-minima.text: Uniform handling of all semantic edge cases — vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents — is a consequence of semantic minimality: because every edge case derives from the same primitives that drive deterministic core semantics, no special-case logic exists.

justifications.label: depth-5 — edge-case uniformity and semantic minimality have a causal relationship: minimality is what makes uniformity possible rather than coincidental

edge-case-uniformity-reinforces-complete.text: Uniform handling of all semantic edge cases — vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents — reinforces the completeness and recoverability of negative semantics: every edge case within the negation lifecycle (missing outlist nodes treated as OUT, challenge of already-justified nodes, recovery from outlist defeat) is handled by the same minimal evaluation rules that ensure reversibility.

justifications.label: Minimality-driven uniformity means negative semantics don't need special-case handling for edge conditions — the same rules that make negation complete also make edge cases uniform

egress-is-resilient-governed-and-self-co.text: All information leaving the system is simultaneously resilient (queries degrade gracefully across all access paths with deterministic output), governed (authorized, budget-constrained, and CI-ready), and serves a self-correcting knowledge base — the system's complete information egress is both trustworthy and operationally sustainable.

justifications.label: Query resilience and output governance jointly ensure trustworthy information egress

empty-antecedents-vacuously-valid.text: An SL justification with an empty antecedent list is valid (vacuous truth via `all([])`), allowing outlist-only justifications to function as "IN unless Y" — used by `challenge` and `supersede` for converted premises

empty-file-is-content-changed-not-delete.text: A zero-byte file that exists on disk is never classified as `source_deleted`; if its hash differs from the stored hash it produces `content_changed`, if it matches it produces no result.

entrenchment-hierarchy-sourced-observati.text: The backtracking entrenchment score encodes a strict priority: sourced premises > unsourced, OBSERVATION type > DERIVED type, and fewer dependents = lower entrenchment (retracted first).

entrenchment-ranks-premises-above-derive.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `add-nogood-retraction-prefers-least-entrenched` and `backtracking-retracts-least-entrenched` which already establish that premises (evidence) are preferred over derived nodes (speculation) during retraction selection.

entrenchment-scoring-uses-weighted-heuri.text: `find_culprits` scores premise candidates for retraction using additive weights: premise +100, has `source` +50, has `source_hash` +25, per-dependent +10, and `beliefs_type` ranges from 10 (NOTE) to 90 (AXIOM/WARNING), preferring retraction of speculative assumptions over evidence.

entrenchment-uses-three-tier-ordering.text: Entrenchment scoring enforces a strict three-tier preference: premises (highest) > source-backed derived nodes (middle) > pure derived nodes (lowest), with dependent count as a tiebreaker within tiers, ensuring `find_culprits` always retracts speculation before evidence.

entry-point-mapping.text: The `reasons` CLI command maps to `reasons_lib.cli:main` via `[project.scripts]` in `pyproject.toml` and is the only registered script entry point.

equilibria-are-negation-transparent-with.text: The system's convergent equilibria simultaneously satisfy two independent completeness criteria: negation transparency (the final stable state is uniquely determined by declarative semantics with no hidden procedural effects from negation) and complete propagation fidelity (every truth change cascades to every transitively dependent node with topology preservation and guided recovery).

justifications.label: Semantic completeness (negation fully resolved) and structural completeness (every dependent reached) together establish that equilibria leave no unresolved state in any dimension

equilibria-are-transparent-and-trajector.text: The system's convergent equilibria are simultaneously negation-transparent (the final stable state is uniquely determined by evaluation rules with complete propagation fidelity) and trajectory-documented (every convergence path generates deterministic traceable events backed by permanent durable audit trails) — convergence is not just mathematically guaranteed but operationally verifiable.

justifications.label: Transparent equilibria plus permanent trajectory documentation yield verifiable convergence

equilibrium-trajectory-is-deterministic-.text: Every convergence trajectory toward an evaluation-invariant equilibrium generates consistently identifiable artifacts with deterministic traceable events, enabling complete post-hoc reconstruction of how each stable state was reached.

justifications.label: Convergence to stable states combined with consistent artifact identification means each equilibrium's history is fully reconstructible

estimate-tokens-chars-div-4.text: `estimate_tokens` uses `len(text) // 4` with a minimum return value of 1; it never returns 0, even for empty strings.

evaluation-is-traceable-and-context-agno.text: Every truth evaluation is simultaneously context-agnostic (producing identical results regardless of evaluation timing, attachment history, or belief origin) and fully traceable (every state change follows a deterministic path recorded in the system's operational history), enabling both reproducibility and post-hoc explanation of any evaluation outcome.

justifications.label: Context-agnostic evaluation (depth-4) and deterministic traceable history (depth-6) from distinct chains combine: you know both WHAT the system computes and WHY each computation occurred

evaluation-is-uniformly-context-and-orig.text: Truth evaluation produces identical results regardless of both attachment history (when/how a justification was added) and structural origin (ordinary belief vs. dialectical construct) — no belief receives special treatment based on provenance, timing, or role in the network.

justifications.label: Context-independence (depth-2) guarantees timing irrelevance while semantic transparency (depth-3) guarantees origin irrelevance; together they close all evaluation-bias vectors.

evaluation-purity-enables-complete-minim.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — is the concrete computational property that makes the completeness-minimality unification possible: purity simultaneously grounds context-agnosticism (enabling the minimal primitive set to handle all cases uniformly) and ensures that architectural completeness follows from rather than despite minimality (because pure evaluation needs no case-specific logic).

justifications.label: Purity is the bridge between the minimal primitive set and complete architectural coverage

evaluation-purity-grounds-agnosticism-an.text: Evaluation purity (uniform, deterministic, no metadata inspection) independently grounds both context-agnosticism (identical results regardless of timing/origin) and semantic minimality (no special-case logic), making them co-occurring consequences of the same architectural choice rather than causally related.

justifications.label: Pure uniform evaluation is the single architectural choice that produces both properties independently

evaluation-purity-grounds-dialectics-thr.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — enables the complete minimal architecture whose negative semantics ground deterministic dialectics, establishing a causal chain from the most fundamental computational property through architectural completeness to dialectical reliability.

justifications.label: Evaluation purity enables architecture and negative semantics ground dialectics; combining reveals the causal chain from the computational foundation (purity) through architecture (completeness via minimality) to the highest-level feature (deterministic dialectics)

evaluation-purity-grounds-governance-tha.text: Evaluation purity provides the semantic foundation for richly governed dialectics while exception safety preserves that rich traceable governance through all failure modes — purity creates the governance properties and exception safety ensures they are never lost, establishing complementary roles in governance assurance.

justifications.label: Purity creates the governance properties, exception safety preserves them through all failure modes

evaluation-traceability-persists-through.text: Every truth evaluation is traceable and context-agnostic from individual computation through system-wide convergence: all structural transformations converge to documented equilibria with deterministic identifiable artifacts, and every evaluation along those convergence trajectories is deterministically reproducible regardless of timing or origin.

justifications.label: Context-agnostic traceable evaluation (depth-7) composes with documented convergent equilibria (depth-9) — traceability persists from individual computations through to final stable states

every-mutation-reports-its-effects.text: All mutating operations report their effects as structured data: retract returns the full changed set, add_justification returns a change dict with old/new truth values, and API mutating operations use before/after truth-value diffing to capture deltas.

justifications.label: Three independent mutation-reporting mechanisms unify into a single observability property — every state change is reported to callers

every-network-mutation-maintains-depende.text: After any public mutation method on `Network` (`add_node`, `retract`, `assert_node`, `add_justification`, `supersede`, `challenge`, `defend`, `convert_to_premise`, `add_nogood`, `summarize`), `verify_dependents()` returns an empty list.

After any public Network mutation (add_node, retract, assert_node, add_justification, supersede, challenge, defend, convert_to_premise, add_nogood, summarize), the dependents index passes `verify_dependents()` — completeness and minimality are maintained incrementally

example-key-absent-when-unspecified.text: Omitting the `example` parameter in `api.add_node` results in the key being entirely absent from `node["metadata"]`, not present as `None` or an empty string.

example-stored-verbatim-in-metadata.text: The `example` field is stored as the exact string provided (no trimming, escaping, or wrapping) and retrieved via `node["metadata"]["example"]` as a flat string value within the metadata JSON blob.

exception-safety-spans-tms-and-source-li.text: The system handles failures safely across both domains: the TMS core resolves exceptional conditions (contradictions via backtracking, challenges via deterministic propagation) while the source integrity pipeline handles its failure modes (missing files, changed content, deleted sources) — no exception in either domain can produce inconsistent or undefined state.

justifications.label: TMS exception safety + fail-safe source lifecycle → unified failure safety across both domains

execution-fallback-chain-three-strategie.text: CLI execution follows a prescribed three-step fallback chain: try the installed `reasons` binary → `cd <repo> && uv run reasons …` → `uvx --from ftl-reasons reasons …`, with the agent trying each in order until one succeeds.

exhaust-implies-auto.text: In `_derive_one_round`, proposals are auto-applied when either `args.auto` or `args.exhaust` is true; the `--exhaust` flag does not require the user to also pass `--auto`.

exhaustive-knowledge-expansion-within-co.text: The system achieves exhaustive knowledge expansion — deterministic reversible reasoning combined with complete LLM-driven derivation with guaranteed termination — within multi-level information boundaries that gate authorization, constrain output size, and defensively validate all ingested beliefs, ensuring unbounded knowledge growth never escapes system controls.

justifications.label: Exhaustive reasoning and derivation combined with multi-level information control ensures knowledge grows without escaping authorization, budget, or validation boundaries

expert-pipeline-extracts-per-document.text: The expert-agent-builder pipeline extracts beliefs per-document (summarize entire document → propose beliefs → record file path), not per-section — the connection between a belief and its source material is a file-level pointer, not a section-level one.

explain-trace-includes-violated-outlist.text: `Network.explain()` returns step dicts that include a `violated_outlist` key (list of IN node IDs) specifically when a justification is defeated by its outlist, in addition to the always-present `outlist` key showing the declared list.

export-api-fault-tolerant-per-node.text: `api.export_api` catches per-node HTTP errors internally, increments an `errors` counter, and continues pushing remaining nodes rather than aborting on the first failure; callers inspect `result["errors"]` rather than catching exceptions.

export-card-belief-counts-are-exhaustive.text: In the EEM card frontmatter, `beliefs_in + beliefs_out == beliefs_total` and `premises + derived == beliefs_total`, where a node is a premise if and only if it has zero justifications.

export-card-defaults-are-explicit.text: `export_card` defaults to `license="mit"`, `domain=[]`, and `base_network=None` when callers omit these parameters; `type` is always the literal string `"eem"` and `schema_version` equals `reasons.metadata.SCHEMA_VERSION`.

export-card-depth-uses-supporting-justif.text: When `supporting_justification` is a valid index, `_node_depth` in `export_card.py` traverses only that single justification's antecedents (the "live" proof path), ignoring sibling justifications; an out-of-range or `None` index falls back to considering all justifications.

export-card-max-depth-is-longest-justifi.text: The "Max derivation depth" reported in the card body equals the length (number of edges) of the longest justification chain in the network; a network with only premises has depth 0.

export-card-partition-is-exhaustive.text: In `export_card`, the node partition is exhaustive: `in_count + out_count == total` (every node is either `"IN"` or not) and `premises + derived == total` (a node is a premise iff it has zero justifications), with no third state.

export-card-title-derived-from-project-n.text: The Markdown H1 title in the card body is produced by applying Python's `.title()` method to the `project_name` value (e.g., `k8s-ops-expert` → `K8S Ops Expert`).

export-import-json-roundtrip-preserves-b.text: The `export_network` → `import_json` pipeline preserves not only structural fidelity (node count, justification structure, outlist entries, metadata) but also behavioral equivalence: defeasible propagation (retract, re-assert, cascade) on the imported database produces identical truth-value outcomes to the source database.

export-markdown-deps-emit-dangling-refs-.text: The `all_deps` collection in `export_markdown` does not guard against antecedent IDs that reference non-existent nodes; a dangling antecedent is emitted as a plain string in the "Depends on" line without crashing, unlike the defeater lookup which uses a `nodes.get()` guard.

export-markdown-orders-in-before-out.text: Within the `## Claims` section of `export_markdown` output, all `[IN]` node entries appear at a lower character offset than any `[OUT]` or `[STALE]` entry.

export-markdown-pg-reconstructs-network.text: The `export_markdown` PostgreSQL path reconstructs a full `Network` object from `export_network()` output — creating Node/Justification objects and wiring the dependents index — because the markdown exporter requires a wired dependency graph, not a flat dict.

export-markdown-section-ordering-is-fixe.text: The document structure follows the fixed order: `# Belief Registry` → `## Claims` (all node entries) → `## Nogoods` (if any nogoods exist); an empty network still emits the section headers.

export-markdown-sort-in-before-out.text: `export_markdown` sorts nodes by the composite key `(truth_value != "IN", id)`, guaranteeing all `IN` nodes appear before all `OUT`/`STALE` nodes with alphabetical tiebreaking — producing deterministic, diff-friendly output.

export-markdown-type-inference-fallback.text: When `node.metadata["beliefs_type"]` is absent or empty, `export_markdown` infers the type as `DERIVED` if the node has at least one justification, or `OBSERVATION` otherwise — ensuring the output always conforms to the beliefs.md schema type token requirement.

export-silently-excludes-restricted-nogo.text: Export operations silently exclude nogoods that reference access-restricted nodes rather than raising a PermissionError, preventing information leakage at the cost of potentially incomplete nogood sets in exported data — this is the deliberate contrast with single-node read commands that do raise.

extensions-compose-transparently-on-core.text: Both extension systems — dialectical challenge/defend and multi-agent federation — compose transparently on the core TMS because each is evaluated by uniform outlist rules, propagated deterministically, reversed by the same primitive, and isolated from the other's namespace.

justifications.label: depth-5 — dialectics and multi-agent are independent extensions that both achieve transparency and safety through the same core mechanisms, demonstrating composability

external-belief-ingestion-is-defensively.text: External beliefs enter the system through defensively-layered pipelines regardless of source: LLM derivation applies fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, and environment isolation, while agent import provides dual reconciliation modes with heterogeneous truth state handling — both converge on the same underlying mutation infrastructure.

justifications.label: depth-2 — two independent ingestion paths (LLM derive, agent import) each have their own defense mechanisms, providing defense in depth for all external input

external-belief-lifecycle-is-complete.text: The system manages external beliefs across their full lifecycle: import/sync provides dual reconciliation modes with heterogeneous truth state handling and namespace auto-wiring, while staleness checking detects source drift for CI gating — beliefs are tracked from initial ingestion through ongoing validity monitoring.

justifications.label: Import reconciliation (depth-2) + staleness CI gate (depth-1) span the full lifecycle, but silent skipping of missing source files creates a gap in drift detection

external-belief-management-is-complete.text: External beliefs are managed across their entire lifecycle with no gap between any management phase: safely integrated through defensive validation pipelines, lifecycle-managed across dual import/sync reconciliation modes, and actively kept current through staleness detection and derive pipeline refresh — providing complete external belief management from ingestion through retirement.

justifications.label: End-to-end external belief management emerges from combining safe-and-current lifecycle properties with safely-integrated ingestion properties, closing the gap between intake and ongoing maintenance

external-beliefs-achieve-integration-par.text: External beliefs achieve full parity with internal beliefs: they are managed across their complete lifecycle with no gap between any management phase AND participate in the same deterministic revision engine as all other belief origins — external provenance is a property of ingestion, not of ongoing maintenance.

justifications.label: Complete lifecycle management (depth-6) combined with origin-agnostic deterministic revision (depth-5) shows external beliefs are first-class citizens with no semantic distinction after ingestion

external-beliefs-achieve-total-integrati.text: External beliefs achieve total integration along all quality axes simultaneously: grounded across every invariant dimension (origin, time, structure), participating in all correction mechanisms with full auditability, and fully equivalent to internal beliefs — no property distinguishes external from internal.

justifications.label: Correctable-and-equivalent (quality parity along revision axes) and fully-invariant-grounded (dimensional coverage) are independently derived from different chains; their conjunction closes all integration gaps.

external-beliefs-are-correctable-and-inv.text: External beliefs achieve full parity along two independent quality axes: invariant equivalence ensures they participate in the same consistency guarantees as internal beliefs, while origin-spanning auditability ensures they are fully correctable with complete traceable history.

justifications.label: External parity extends from invariant equivalence to correction auditability — no second-class beliefs

external-beliefs-are-defended-and-lifecy.text: External beliefs are managed end-to-end across a complete trust boundary: defensively contained at ingestion through layered validation pipelines and namespace isolation, then actively lifecycle-managed through dual reconciliation modes, staleness detection against source material, and CI gating — no phase of external belief existence lacks oversight.

justifications.label: Defensive ingestion plus ongoing lifecycle management yields complete external trust boundary

external-beliefs-are-fully-invariant-gro.text: External beliefs achieve complete invariant equivalence with internal beliefs, and those invariants are anchored along all three dimensions — origin, temporal, and structural — meaning external integration participates in the system's deepest invariant guarantees, not merely surface-level safety.

justifications.label: External equivalence combined with triple-dimensional invariant grounding yields complete external invariant coverage

external-beliefs-are-invariant-equivalen.text: External beliefs achieve complete equivalence with internal beliefs at every system level: they participate in identical invariant-preserving revision systems and achieve full behavioral integration parity — the system provides no mechanism to distinguish external from internal beliefs in terms of protection or management.

justifications.label: Invariant-protection parity plus behavioral integration parity yields full external/internal belief equivalence

external-beliefs-are-safe-and-current.text: External beliefs are managed end-to-end across their complete lifecycle with no gap between ingestion safety and ongoing maintenance: defensively contained at ingestion through layered validation, correctly lifecycle-managed through import reconciliation and staleness checking, and actively tracked for currency — no external belief enters unvalidated, drifts undetected, or persists without lifecycle oversight.

justifications.label: ingestion defense + currency tracking = complete external belief management (depth-5 GATE from depth-4 + depth-3 GATE)

external-beliefs-defensively-contained.text: External beliefs pass through two independent safety layers: defensive ingestion pipelines (fail-soft validation, Jaccard guards, dual import/sync reconciliation modes) filter and validate beliefs on entry, while the self-contained agent subsystem (namespace isolation, relay-pair kill-switches, reversible lifecycle management) constrains their operational footprint after ingestion.

justifications.label: Ingestion defense guards the entry boundary; containment guards the operational boundary — defense in depth for external beliefs

external-deps-become-premises.text: A claim whose `depends_on` references are all absent from the beliefs file gets no justifications and is added as a premise (IN by default).

external-ingestion-is-format-resilient-a.text: External belief ingestion achieves both defensive containment (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, dual import/sync reconciliation, namespace isolation) AND format resilience (parser version fallback, forward-compatible metadata parsing, prose-tolerant JSON extraction), ensuring robust integration even as external source formats evolve unpredictably.

justifications.label: Defensive ingestion pipelines and format-resilient parsers are complementary — one handles malicious/invalid input, the other handles legitimate format variation

external-ingestion-is-resilient-and-conv.text: External belief ingestion achieves end-to-end reliability through two complementary properties: format resilience absorbs syntactic variation at the parsing boundary (dual parser versions, schema migration tolerance, prose-tolerant JSON extraction with defensive layering), while deterministic convergence ensures consistent final state through fixpoint reconciliation regardless of input ordering or repeated application.

justifications.label: Connects orphaned depth-3 format-resilience belief with convergence to show parsing variation does not prevent deterministic stable outcomes

external-inputs-face-defense-in-depth.text: External beliefs face defense in depth across two independent containment layers: input-level containment (defensive validation pipelines, agent namespace isolation) prevents bad data from entering, while system-level containment (architectural layer boundaries, lifecycle-aware checking and propagation) prevents bad data from persisting or spreading.

justifications.label: depth-4 — input containment and system containment are independent and complementary: even if one layer is bypassed, the other catches violations

external-integration-is-architecturally-.text: External beliefs are end-to-end safe within the system's architecture: defensively contained at ingestion and lifecycle-managed thereafter (external belief thread) within the same three-layer boundaries and atomic mutation guarantees that protect internal operations (architecture thread).

justifications.label: External belief safety (depth-4) and architectural safety (depth-3) are from completely independent antecedent chains; their conjunction shows external beliefs inherit the same architectural guarantees as internal operations, gated on ingestion-related defects being resolved

external-integration-is-hardened-and-bou.text: LLM integration achieves production-grade robustness (bounded execution, fail-soft error handling, process isolation, fault tolerance) while information boundaries are controlled at every level (authorization gating, budget constraints, defensive ingestion) — the system neither leaks sensitive information outward nor admits unvalidated beliefs inward.

justifications.label: Both depth-5 beliefs are currently unused as antecedents; combining LLM hardening with information boundary control yields bidirectional integration safety

metadata.retract_reason: Invalid: controlled mechanisms don't entail zero-leakage guarantees

external-integration-preserves-all-invar.text: External beliefs are architecturally safe at ingestion and participate in the same invariant-preserving revision system as all other belief origins — architectural containment and revision parity together ensure external integration cannot corrupt system invariants.

justifications.label: architectural safety plus revision parity closes the invariant gap for external beliefs

external-interface-is-bidirectionally-bo.text: The system's interaction with external systems is bounded in both directions: output is budget-limited through accurate token estimation ensuring context windows are respected, and input drift is comprehensively detected through staleness checking — no unbounded data flows cross the system boundary.

justifications.label: Depth-2 — output bounding (compact) and input monitoring (staleness) together characterize the system's complete external interface as fully managed

metadata.retract_reason: review-beliefs: Staleness checking detects that input has changed but does not bound input — detection is not constraint; additionally the claim attributes "accurate token estimation" to compact but its own antecedent does not establish estimation accuracy.

external-lifecycle-achieves-topology-acc.text: External beliefs receive quality-complete self-correction that operates on accurate convergent topology — every correction to an externally-originated belief propagates through verified dependency structure with complete fidelity, ensuring external belief quality is maintained with the same topological accuracy as internal beliefs.

justifications.label: External beliefs receive topology-accurate quality-complete correction — no fidelity gap between internal and external correction paths

external-lifecycle-is-complete-and-autom.text: External beliefs achieve both complete lifecycle management (dual reconciliation modes with heterogeneous truth state handling and staleness detection) and automated ongoing maintenance (idempotent sync with cascade preservation and full source staleness coverage), enabling zero-touch external belief management

justifications.label: Complete lifecycle plus automated sync enables zero-touch management — blocked by silent missing-file handling

external-lifecycle-is-deterministic-and-.text: External beliefs follow a fully deterministic lifecycle from ingestion through ongoing maintenance, enclosed within verified trust boundaries at every phase: structural verification with trust-bounded bidirectional flow control at the perimeter, and deterministic architecturally-grounded lifecycle management governing internal state trajectories.

justifications.label: External perimeter trust boundaries (depth-9) combined with deterministic lifecycle management (depth-6) from independent architectural chains ensures external beliefs follow predictable paths within verified perimeters

external-lifecycle-operates-within-rich-.text: External beliefs achieve complete automated lifecycle management within a metadata-enabled source-grounded governance framework — creation, reconciliation, staleness detection, and ongoing maintenance all operate under rich governance extending beyond binary truth values to structured lifecycle state.

justifications.label: External lifecycle completeness operates within metadata-enabled governance, not independently of it

external-lifecycle-receives-quality-comp.text: External beliefs follow deterministic trust-bounded lifecycles AND receive self-correction that is complete across all quality dimensions — grounded in source integrity, documented with referenceable artifacts, convergent on accurate topology, and evolution-tolerant — ensuring external beliefs are not merely contained but actively maintained at the same quality standard as internal beliefs.

justifications.label: External lifecycle determinism combined with quality-complete self-correction — external beliefs get full-spectrum maintenance, not just containment

external-surface-is-fully-controlled.text: The system's external surface is fully controlled along independent axes: bidirectional bounds constrain output size (token budgets) and input quality (staleness detection), while defensive containment layers (validation pipelines, namespace isolation) prevent external beliefs from violating internal invariants.

justifications.label: Bidirectional I/O bounding and defensive containment together control the full external surface (depth-4)

external-surface-is-verified-and-trust-b.text: The complete external-facing surface achieves both structural verification (pure delegation with hermetic tests and fault tolerance across all information paths) and comprehensive trust enforcement (architectural self-containment with information flow control at every boundary) — no external interaction bypasses either the verification chain or trust controls.

justifications.label: Verified fault-tolerant interface + comprehensive trust boundaries means the external surface has no unverified or unbounded interaction path

external-surface-is-verified-trust-bound.text: The system's complete external perimeter achieves defense-in-depth through three independently-established properties: structural verification (pure delegation with hermetic tests), trust boundaries (self-containment and defensive ingestion), and bidirectional flow control (token budgets constraining output, hardened LLM integration constraining input) — no external interaction bypasses all three layers.

justifications.label: Verification ensures correctness, trust bounds prevent escalation, and bidirectional control constrains volume — three independent perimeter defenses from two convergent chains

extract-tool-call-is-tool-name-agnostic.text: `extract_tool_call` parses any valid `{"tool": "<name>", ...}` JSON object regardless of the tool name — there is no allow-list restricting which tools can be dispatched.

extract-tool-call-returns-first-match.text: When LLM output contains multiple JSON objects with a `"tool"` key, `extract_tool_call()` returns only the first valid match and ignores the rest; malformed JSON lines are silently skipped.

extract-tool-call-schema-agnostic.text: Covered by existing `extract-tool-call-returns-first-match` and `ask-uses-text-based-tool-protocol` which together establish that tool call parsing is generic.

extras-map-one-to-one-to-modules.text: Each optional dependency group maps 1:1 to a specific module: `pg` extra gates `reasons_lib/pg.py`, `cluster` extra gates `reasons_lib/cluster.py`, and `test-pg` is a superset combining `pg` and `test`.

fault-tolerance-spans-inspection-through.text: Fault tolerance covers the complete belief quality spectrum: passive inspection operations (review, staleness checking, list-negative classification) degrade gracefully with fail-safe defaults and never mutate state, AND active self-correction (contradiction resolution via backtracking, staleness detection via source hashing) continues operating without external LLM dependencies — the system maintains quality assurance autonomously even when LLMs, external files, or network resources are unavailable.

justifications.label: Passive inspection fault tolerance and active self-correction LLM resilience together ensure the system has a degraded-but-functional quality mode under any external failure

fetch-export-maps-http-errors-to-runtime.text: `fetch_export` raises `RuntimeError` with a domain-specific message for expected HTTP failures (401 → "Authentication failed", 404 → "Agent not found"), making it a "loud" low-level function contrasted with the "quiet" aggregate-level `import_api`/`export_api`.

fetch-export-returns-unparsed-string.text: `fetch_export` returns the HTTP response body as a raw UTF-8 string without calling `json.loads`; the caller (`api.py`) is responsible for deserialization, keeping the function format-agnostic.

format-resilience-spans-all-external-int.text: The system tolerates format variation at every external interface — derive output parsers support version fallback, import parsers silently skip unknown fields, storage handles schema evolution — and extends this resilience to LLM response parsing, where the list-negative parser uses regex extraction to recover structured data from prose-laden responses.

justifications.label: Format evolution tolerance extends from system boundaries to LLM output parsing

format-resilient-boundaries-enforce-vali.text: All system boundaries simultaneously tolerate format variation at every level — from LLM response parsing through schema migration to derive output versioning — while enforcing strict validated trust through typed exceptions, referential integrity checks, and hallucination filtering.

justifications.label: Format resilience (including list-negative prose-tolerant parsing) composes with strict validation and evolution tolerance — flexibility and correctness coexist at every boundary

forward-references-are-silently-tolerate.text: Covered by existing `outlist-absent-means-out` (missing outlist nodes treated as OUT) and `active-not-in-antecedents` (missing antecedents treated as not-IN), which together describe the forward-reference tolerance behavior.

frontmatter-values-are-strings-even-for-.text: The `strip_frontmatter()` parser always returns frontmatter values as strings (e.g., `"node_count": "42"` rather than `42`), and single-quoted values have their quotes stripped.

ftl-reasons-zero-runtime-deps.text: The core `reasons_lib` package has no mandatory runtime dependencies — all external packages (psycopg, sentence-transformers, scikit-learn, mcp) are gated behind optional install extras (`[pg]`, `[cluster]`, `[mcp]`).

fts-errors-silently-caught-in-search.text: FTS5 query errors in `_fts_search` are silently caught and return an empty list, falling back to substring matching — the only place in the API where errors are deliberately swallowed (FTS5 table may not exist).

fts-progressive-relaxation.text: When a multi-term FTS query returns no results, the search engine progressively drops terms until it finds matches or exhausts all subsets.

fts-relaxation-bounded.text: Progressive FTS query relaxation is bounded: a 20-term query produces at most 51 `_fts_query` invocations, preventing unbounded search expansion on long input queries.

fts-relaxation-budget-caps-at-50.text: Progressive FTS5 search relaxation — dropping query terms via combinations when the full-term query returns no results — is capped at `_MAX_RELAXATION_QUERIES` (50) to prevent combinatorial blowup on many-term queries.

fts-relaxation-capped-at-fifty-queries.text: `_fts_search` caps progressive term relaxation at 50 FTS5 queries to prevent combinatorial explosion on long search inputs, dropping terms one at a time via `combinations` down to `len(terms) // 2`.

fts-stop-words-filtered-before-query.text: FTS queries filter a `_STOP_WORDS` frozenset before querying FTS5; if all terms are stop words, the search falls back to terms longer than 1 character.

fts5-index-is-content-backed.text: The `chunks_fts` virtual table is created with `content=chunks, content_rowid=id`, meaning FTS5 stores only the inverted index and all row data (filename, section, cluster) must be read back from the `chunks` content table via JOIN.

full-system-integrity-is-gap-free.text: The system achieves gap-free integrity — enforced across all architectural layers, lifecycle states, and mutation paths — only when the dependents reverse index is reliably maintained and propagation handles dangling references gracefully.

justifications.label: depth-4 gate — both antecedents implicitly assume a well-formed dependents graph; the fragile denormalization and unchecked lookup are the two known gaps that could break this assumption

full-user-stack-is-verified-atomic-deleg.text: The full user-facing stack forms a verified chain of atomic delegation: the CLI is structurally pure delegation verified through hermetic integration tests, and every mutation flowing through the API layer is atomic, audited, and produces observable before/after diffs — ensuring end-to-end traceability from user command to persisted state change.

justifications.label: CLI verification (depth-3) and mutation observability (depth-2) combine into the emergent property that the entire user-facing stack is both verified and transparent

fully-characterized-loop-sustains-indefi.text: The fully characterized self-maintaining loop — origin-agnostic, fully observable, and minimality-sustained — can operate without temporal bound because its self-correction is resource-sustainable within a deterministic, structurally sound lifecycle; characterization completeness combined with resource sustainability yields indefinite operability.

justifications.label: Connects the depth-7 leaf (indefinite sustainability) with the depth-10 full characterization — the characterized loop doesn't just describe what the system does, but guarantees it can do so forever

gate-belief-semantics-are-conjunctive-wi.text: A gated (GATE) belief is IN if and only if all its antecedents are IN AND no unless/outlist node is IN; retracting an outlist node restores the gated belief to IN.

generator-stamp-contains-ftl-reasons-pre.text: The `generator` metadata field always contains the substring `"ftl-reasons/"` followed by a version number — it is a provenance stamp present in all export formats (JSON, Markdown, SQLite).

git-fail-open-assumes-changed.text: All git-checking functions (`file_changed_since`, `file_lines_changed_since`) return `True` (assume file changed) on any subprocess error, non-zero exit code, or timeout, forcing fallback to full content-hash comparison rather than silently marking a node as fresh.

git-operations-require-git-binary-on-pat.text: Git-aware pinning (`get_file_commit_sha`, `file_changed_since`, `file_lines_changed_since`) shells out via `subprocess` to `git log` and `git diff` rather than using a git library, making a working `git` binary on `PATH` a runtime requirement for the fast path.

gitignore-covers-internal-tooling.text: The presence of `.sdlc-loop/` and `.code-expert/` entries is a trivial listing of internal tooling directories; it does not constrain how a developer writes code, configures the project, or reasons about system behavior.

gitignore-permits-no-exception-commits.text: The `.gitignore` contains no negation (`!`) patterns, meaning any file matching an ignore rule (e.g., `*.db`, `network.json`) cannot be committed via normal `git add` without `-f`, and test fixtures must avoid excluded extensions like `.db`.

gitignore-uses-unanchored-patterns.text: The observation that patterns lack a leading `/` is an implementation detail of the `.gitignore` syntax, not an architectural invariant or behavioral contract a developer needs to know to work in the codebase.

governance-achieves-topology-and-source-.text: Rich governance — deterministic, exception-safe, and source-grounded with topology-complete transitions — simultaneously achieves gap-free source coverage, ensuring governance completeness along two independent dimensions: propagation reach (every state change reaches all transitively dependent nodes) and integrity coverage (every source file is tracked with no silent gaps).

justifications.label: governance complete across both propagation-reach and source-integrity dimensions

governance-and-dialectics-have-verified-.text: Complete governance across topology, source, and traceability with dually-grounded dialectical operations achieves verified reference integrity at all node ID boundaries — governance completeness and dialectical assurance are not only independently established but reference-verified.

justifications.label: governance completeness + dialectical assurance with reference verification, gated on audit issue #126

governance-assurance-is-universal-and-se.text: Every belief modification achieves governance assurance that is itself dialectically assured and dually grounded — the governance framework constraining all modifications is verified by the same dialectical and grounding mechanisms it employs, creating a self-reinforcing quality guarantee at the system's highest abstraction level.

justifications.label: Governance that assures modifications is itself assured by the same mechanisms, closing the self-verification loop

governance-completeness-is-dually-ground.text: Complete governance across topology, source, and traceability dimensions rests on two independent grounding chains (evaluation purity and edge-case uniformity), so no single semantic foundation failure can undermine the governance framework's three-dimensional completeness guarantees.

justifications.label: three-dimensional completeness + dual grounding = governance resilient to single-foundation failure

governance-determinism-is-generated-and-.text: Governance determinism has a complete lifecycle: it is generated as an emergent consequence of minimality (not independently engineered) through source integrity, and simultaneously preserved through exception safety underpinned by evaluation purity — minimality produces the determinism, purity grounds the governance it enables, and exception safety ensures that governance survives all failure modes.

justifications.label: determinism generated by minimality + preserved by purity/exception-safety = complete property lifecycle

governance-determinism-is-minimality-eme.text: Rich governance achieves end-to-end determinism spanning revision semantics through source integrity, and this determinism is itself an emergent consequence of unified minimality, completeness, and determinism rather than an independently-engineered property — the same minimal foundations that produce governance completeness also produce its end-to-end deterministic reach.

justifications.label: End-to-end determinism (revision through source) emerges from the same unified minimality that produces governance completeness

governance-has-dual-independent-groundin.text: The system's governance framework receives assurance from two fully independent grounding chains: dialectical operations are grounded by evaluation purity and semantic uniformity, while the rich governance framework itself is grounded by determinism, exception safety, and source integrity — five independent assurance dimensions from orthogonal chains.

justifications.label: Two orthogonal chains (dialectical grounding and governance grounding) contribute five independent assurance dimensions

governance-is-dialectically-assured-and-.text: Governance completeness — spanning topology, source, and traceability dimensions — is simultaneously dialectically assured through complete bidirectional operations (forward reliability and backward recovery with dual semantic grounding) and independently grounded through two evaluation chains (purity and uniformity), achieving both operational confidence and epistemic independence

justifications.label: Combining the two depth-13 IN terminals — dialectical assurance provides operational confidence while dual grounding provides epistemic independence from the same governance foundation

governance-is-topology-source-and-tracea.text: Rich governance simultaneously achieves completeness across three independent output dimensions — topology-complete in reach, source-verified in integrity, and metadata-enriched in traceability — so every governance action produces a verifiable, traceable, source-grounded state transition.

justifications.label: Unifies what governance covers (topology + source) with what it produces (rich traceable state) into three-dimensional completeness

governance-topology-is-reference-verifie.text: Rich governance's topology-complete transitions and metadata-governed bidirectional modifications have fully verified reference integrity at all system boundaries — no node ID reference bypasses validation at any boundary — when the reference validation audit confirms coverage at the three identified boundary gaps (issue #126).

justifications.label: topology-complete governance achieves reference-verified status after audit

graph-traversal-is-complete-and-terminat.text: Both forward truth propagation and backward retraction cascades achieve complete graph traversal (reaching all transitively affected nodes through all relationship types including outlists) with guaranteed termination, ensuring the system converges from both assertion and retraction operations.

justifications.label: Forward propagation is topology-complete even under graph inconsistency; backward retraction is transitive and terminating — together they show all graph traversal is both complete and bounded regardless of direction.

grounded-dialectics-achieve-complete-bid.text: Dialectical operations achieve both semantic grounding (through evaluation purity and uniform semantics) and operational completeness (forward reliability of challenge/defend with backward recovery of defeat reversal) — grounding ensures the operations are well-founded while bidirectional reliability ensures they work correctly in both directions.

justifications.label: Dialectics are simultaneously grounded (purity + uniformity) and operationally complete (forward + backward)

growth-converges-with-topology-and-assur.text: Knowledge growth simultaneously preserves universal multidimensional assurance and converges deterministically with topology preservation and guided recovery — the expanding knowledge base reaches stable states where all structural relationships are maintained and all safety guarantees hold, regardless of the modification path taken.

justifications.label: Exhaustive growth preserving assurance + deterministic convergence with topology means growth never destabilizes the network

growth-preserves-universal-assurance.text: The system grows its knowledge base exhaustively — through deterministic reasoning and LLM-driven derivation with guaranteed termination — while simultaneously maintaining universal multidimensional operational assurance spanning temporal self-correction, end-to-end reliability, and information flow control; growth never compromises any assurance dimension.

justifications.label: Exhaustive information-governed growth (depth-8) combined with universal multidimensional assurance (depth-8) shows the system can expand without degrading any reliability axis

hash-file-full-sha256.text: `hash_file` returns a full 64-character hex SHA-256 digest (per the fix in PR #40 that removed the earlier `[:16]` truncation).

hash-file-import-unused.text: Trivial/unstable detail about an unused import; not a meaningful architectural invariant.

hash-sources-additive-unless-forced.text: `hash_sources` only fills nodes with an empty `source_hash`; it never overwrites an existing non-empty hash unless `force=True` is explicitly passed.

hash-sources-idempotent-without-force.text: `hash_sources` with default `force=False` skips nodes that already have a `source_hash`, making repeated backfill calls safe; `force=True` rehashes unconditionally.

hash-sources-is-additive-by-default.text: `hash_sources` without `force=True` never overwrites an existing non-empty `source_hash`; it only backfills nodes with empty or missing hashes.

hash-sources-mutates-network.text: `hash_sources` writes directly to `node.source_hash` on the in-memory network, while `check_stale` is purely read-only — an intentional asymmetry.

hash-sources-no-overwrite-default.text: `hash_sources` with `force=False` (the default) only backfills missing hashes and will never modify a node that already has a `source_hash` value.

hash-truncation-is-16-hex.text: Source hashes are SHA-256 truncated to the first 16 hex characters (64 bits), reducing collision resistance to ~32 bits for birthday attacks compared to the full 256-bit hash.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #40

hf-401-always-maps-to-authentication-run.text: A 401 HTTP response from any HuggingFace API call (create_repo or upload_file) is mapped to `RuntimeError` with a message matching "Authentication failed"; callers never see a raw `HTTPError`.

hf-create-repo-409-is-idempotent.text: A 409 HTTP response from the HF "create repo" endpoint is swallowed and treated as success (the repo already exists), making `publish_hf` safe to invoke repeatedly against the same repo name.

hf-download-hardcoded-path.text: `download_network` in `reasons/hf.py` always fetches `network.json` from the `main` branch of the resolved repo (URL: `{org}/{name}/resolve/main/network.json`); there is no parameter to select a different branch or filename.

hf-download-translates-http-errors-to-ru.text: `download_network` converts raw `urllib` `HTTPError` exceptions into higher-level `RuntimeError` with actionable messages (401 → "Authentication required", 404 → "not found"), so callers of `api.import_hf` never encounter `HTTPError` directly.

hf-publish-uploads-exactly-three-files.text: `api.publish_hf` uploads precisely three files — `network.json`, `beliefs.md`, and `README.md` — to the target HF repo's `main` branch, and performs exactly four HTTP calls (one create + three uploads).

hf-repo-id-normalization-with-env-overri.text: `resolve_repo_id` in `reasons/hf.py` normalizes bare names by prepending `DEFAULT_HF_ORG` (`"EEM-Hub"`), which is overridable via the `REASONS_HF_ORG` environment variable; explicit `org/name` and full-URL forms pass through unchanged.

hf-resolve-repo-id-preserves-explicit-or.text: `resolve_repo_id` prepends the default org (`EEM-Hub` or `REASONS_HF_ORG` env var) only to bare names without a `/`; an explicit `org/name` string or full URL is passed through unchanged.

hf-token-resolution-chain.text: Token resolution in `reasons/hf.py` follows a strict priority chain: explicit argument → `HF_TOKEN` environment variable → `~/.cache/huggingface/token` file → `None`, mirroring `huggingface-cli` credential behavior so existing logged-in users work without passing `--token`.

hf-token-resolution-follows-param-env-fi.text: The HF token is resolved in order: explicit `token` parameter → `HF_TOKEN` environment variable → `~/.huggingface/token` file; if none is found, a `RuntimeError` is raised before any network call is made.

hf-token-resolution-priority-chain.text: `_resolve_token` follows a strict priority order: explicit argument > `HF_TOKEN` environment variable > `~/.cache/huggingface/token` file > `None`; an explicit token always shadows the environment variable regardless of whether the env var is set.

hf-write-ops-require-caller-provided-tok.text: `create_repo` and `upload_file` in `reasons/hf.py` do NOT call `_resolve_token` internally — the caller must pass a non-`None` token — while `download_network` tolerates `None` (for public repos), creating an asymmetry between read and write paths.

hints-exclude-directly-retracted-node.text: The node passed to `retract_node` never appears in the `restoration_hints` list — only cascade victims with surviving premises do.

idempotent-reimport-skips-all.text: Covered by existing `import-skips-existing-sync-is-remote-wins` which captures the idempotent import behavior

identity-transformation-is-complete-and-.text: Premise identity is bidirectionally transformable (challenge destroys premise identity, convert-to-premise restores it) and the destructive direction achieves full reliability through crash-safe semantics-preserving propagation — making identity transformation a complete and reliable lifecycle operation in both directions.

justifications.label: Bidirectional transformability establishes completeness while crash-safe reliable dialectics establish correctness; together they ensure identity transformation is fully trustworthy

identity-transformation-is-semantically-.text: Challenge creates an irreversible structural transformation (premise → justified node), yet the resulting dialectical structure receives identical evaluation to any other belief — the permanent identity change has no lasting semantic consequence because evaluation is uniformly origin-agnostic and context-independent.

justifications.label: Architectural asymmetry (depth-4) establishes that identity loss is permanent; semantic transparency (depth-3) establishes that evaluation is indifferent to it — the "damage" is structurally real but semantically invisible.

identity-transformation-operates-within-.text: All premise identity transformations — irreversible dialectical challenge and restorative conversion — operate within reproducible, boundary-safe deterministic reasoning, ensuring that structural changes to belief identity follow predictable, evolution-tolerant paths and produce verifiable results.

justifications.label: Identity transformation reliability combined with deterministic reasoning boundary safety — even irreversible structural changes are reproducible

import-achieves-ordered-convergent-recon.text: Import achieves correct final state through two reinforcing mechanisms: deliberate ordering discipline (add → propagate → retract) ensures deferred retractions don't corrupt intermediate states, while deterministic convergence (dual reconciliation modes reaching stable states, propagation terminating via fixpoint) ensures the result is unique and reproducible regardless of input ordering within each phase.

justifications.label: Ordering (depth-1) prevents phase-interaction bugs; convergence (depth-3) prevents input-order sensitivity — together they make import deterministic at both the macro (phase) and micro (within-phase) levels.

import-agent-active-premise-carries-role.text: The synthetic `<agent>:active` premise node created by `import_agent` carries `role=agent_premise` in its metadata, distinguishing it from user-authored premises and enabling programmatic identification of infrastructure nodes.

import-agent-deferred-retraction.text: Nodes that should be OUT are first created as IN (so they participate in dependency registration), collected in `retract_after`, and retracted only after `recompute_all()` — ordering matters for correct graph construction.

import-agent-dual-format-parity.text: `import_agent` accepts both Markdown and JSON source files and produces structurally and behaviorally equivalent network states, with the JSON path explicitly preserving the full justification array (antecedents, outlist, type, label).

import-agent-inactive-always-in-outlist.text: Every imported belief unconditionally has `agent:inactive` in its outlist, enforced in `_build_justifications()` with no code path that omits it — this is the mechanism behind the per-agent kill switch.

import-agent-inactive-never-in-anteceden.text: Duplicates the existing belief `kill-switch-uses-outlist-not-antecedent` — the "not antecedent" half is already captured.

import-agent-infra-nodes-excluded-from-r.text: `_sync_claims()` filters out infrastructure nodes (active/inactive) via `infra_ids` before computing the removal set, so the kill-switch pair is never retracted by remote-wins sync.

import-agent-namespace-prefix.text: Every node imported from agent X gets the ID prefix `X:`, including infrastructure nodes `X:active` and `X:inactive`, ensuring zero collision with local or other-agent beliefs

import-agent-normalization-diverges-on-o.text: `_normalize_markdown` drops all justifications for OUT nodes (sets to empty list), while `_normalize_json` preserves the full justification structure including outlists — meaning the shared `_import_claims`/`_sync_claims` logic receives structurally different data depending on source format.

import-agent-normalizers-share-intermedi.text: Both `_normalize_markdown()` and `_normalize_json()` produce identical intermediate dicts (id, text, is_out, source, source_hash, date, metadata, raw_justifications) before hitting shared `_import_claims`/`_sync_claims` logic.

import-agent-out-beliefs-get-empty-justi.text: Beliefs that are OUT or STALE in the source are imported with empty justification lists, preventing `recompute_all` from resurrecting them to IN.

import-agent-out-beliefs-not-resurrected.text: Beliefs marked OUT or STALE in the source are imported as OUT and are never resurrected by `recompute_all`, even when their justification antecedents are all IN in the local database.

import-agent-retraction-survives-recompu.text: After retracting an imported belief, `recompute_all()` must not resurrect it — the justification structure must not provide alternative paths to IN (issue #16 regression invariant).

import-agent-silently-filters-invalid-re.text: `reasons/import_agent.py` raises no exceptions for normal operational issues: missing outlist/antecedent IDs are silently filtered during normalization, nogoods with <2 valid nodes are skipped, and topo-sort cycles are force-appended rather than raised.

import-agent-topo-sort-breaks-cycles.text: `_topo_sort_claims` breaks dependency cycles by appending all remaining unsorted nodes after `max_passes = len(remaining) + 1` iterations rather than raising an error, ensuring import always completes.

import-beliefs-derived-type-maps-to-sing.text: During `import_into_network`, claims with type `DERIVED` receive exactly one SL justification whose `antecedents` list matches the source document's "Depends on" field, establishing the dependency relationship in the network graph.

import-beliefs-nogood-id-uses-high-water.text: `_next_nogood_id` is set to `max(current, parsed_id + 1)` during import, preventing future auto-generated nogood IDs from colliding with imported ones.

import-beliefs-observation-type-maps-to-.text: During `import_into_network`, claims with type `OBSERVATION` are imported as premises with an empty `justifications` list, making them un-defeatable root nodes whose truth value can only change via explicit retraction.

import-beliefs-parser-is-forward-compati.text: Unknown `- ` metadata lines in belief markdown are silently skipped via a `pass` branch, making the parser forward-compatible with new export format fields.

import-beliefs-path-import-unused.text: Vestigial import detail — too trivial and unstable to track as a belief; it could be cleaned up at any time.

import-beliefs-raises-no-exceptions.text: `import_into_network` and all its helpers (`parse_beliefs`, `parse_nogoods`, `parse_repos`, topo-sort) never raise in the normal code path; the returned summary dict (`claims_skipped`, `nogoods_imported`, etc.) is the sole error-reporting channel.

import-functions-parse-before-dispatch.text: API import functions (`import_json`, `import_beliefs`, `import_agent`) read and parse files into structured data in the API layer before delegating to `PgApi` — PgApi never receives raw file paths

import-handles-heterogeneous-truth-state.text: The import pipeline handles mixed truth states: OUT/STALE beliefs arrive without justifications, topological sort tolerates cycles, and two-phase truth maintenance reconciles everything post-import

justifications.label: Three independent robustness mechanisms ensure import succeeds regardless of source network state

import-json-missing-file-raises-filenotf.text: `api.import_json` raises `FileNotFoundError` when the specified path does not exist, rather than silently returning an empty import result — the error contract distinguishes "file not found" from "file had no nodes."

import-json-uses-topological-sort.text: `api.import_json()` reconstructs networks via a multi-pass topological sort loop — repeatedly adding nodes whose dependencies are already loaded — with a force-add fallback for cycles or missing deps.

import-ordering-ensures-correct-final-st.text: Import follows a deliberate ordering discipline — add nodes first, propagate truth values second, apply explicit retractions last — ensuring deferred retractions correctly override any truth values that propagation would compute, producing a final state that respects both structural dependencies and explicit intent.

justifications.label: The two-phase structure and deferred retraction ordering interact to guarantee correct final truth values

import-paths-bump-nogood-counter.text: Both `import_json` and `import_into_network` update `_next_nogood_id` to at least `max_imported_id + 1`, ensuring imported nogoods with explicit IDs don't create future collisions

import-provides-complete-reconciliation.text: The import subsystem provides complete reconciliation coverage: heterogeneous truth states are handled correctly on initial load, dual modes support additive import and remote-wins sync for different operational needs, and the colon-based namespace convention with auto-wiring prevents ID collisions across agents.

justifications.label: Import handles all truth states, sync handles ongoing updates, and namespacing prevents cross-agent collisions

import-reconciliation-converges-determin.text: Import reconciliation achieves both completeness and convergence: dual import/sync modes handle heterogeneous truth states with namespace isolation and topological cycle tolerance (completeness), while all reconciliation operations — individual propagation, agent sync, and global recompute — converge to deterministic fixed points on repeated application (convergence), ensuring that import never introduces oscillation or nondeterminism.

justifications.label: Complete reconciliation without deterministic convergence risks oscillation; convergence without completeness risks missing cases — together they guarantee stable, thorough import

import-skips-existing-sync-is-remote-win.text: Import mode (`import_agent`) is a one-time load that skips existing nodes; sync mode updates text/justifications/truth values with remote-wins semantics and retracts locally any beliefs removed from the remote

import-sync-has-dual-reconciliation-mode.text: The import/sync subsystem offers two distinct reconciliation strategies: import is additive (skips existing nodes), while sync is remote-wins (overwrites text, justifications, and truth values from the remote source).

justifications.label: The two modes represent a clear design choice between preserving local state (import) and trusting the remote source (sync)

import-sync-roundtrip-form-lossless-exte.text: The import→sync→export pipeline is lossless at every boundary: import tolerates missing metadata and topological cycles gracefully, sync preserves cascade structure with remote-wins reconciliation, and export/import roundtrips preserve behavioral equivalence including retraction and stale-reason state — external networks can be ingested, reconciled, and re-exported without semantic loss.

justifications.label: Each antecedent independently guarantees one boundary is lossless (ingestion tolerance, cycle handling, cascade preservation, roundtrip equivalence, retraction fidelity); the unified claim is end-to-end external interface losslessness.
