import-tolerates-absent-metadata-without.text: Both JSON import (missing `"meta"` key) and Markdown import (missing YAML frontmatter) succeed with defaults rather than raising — the system must never crash on files written by older versions that lack the metadata envelope.

import-topo-sort-cycle-tolerant.text: Topological sorting of imported claims is best-effort: cycles cause remaining nodes to be appended in arbitrary order rather than raising an error, a pragmatic choice that avoids crashing on circular references.

import-topo-sort-tolerates-cycles.text: `_topo_sort_claims` attempts topological ordering but appends remaining nodes when progress stalls, gracefully handling dependency cycles instead of erroring

import-two-phase-truth-maintenance.text: Import/sync adds all nodes first, then runs `recompute_all()` to propagate truth values, then performs explicit retractions — this ordering prevents incorrect cascades from partially-constructed networks

import-wires-reverse-index.text: Covered by existing `dependents-is-manual-reverse-index` which captures that the reverse index is manually maintained

importers-still-use-legacy-path.text: Seven internal modules under `reasons/` (`ask.py`, `cli.py`, `contradictions.py`, `derive.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `pg.py`, `repair.py`) and 50+ test files still import via `reasons_lib.api`, making the shim load-bearing until every one of those imports is migrated to `reasons.api`.

incremental-propagation-is-fully-complet.text: Incremental truth propagation reaches every node whose truth value should change — including nodes that depend via outlist entries — without requiring periodic full recomputation, because safe terminating BFS traversal operates over a dependents index that tracks both antecedent and outlist relationships.

justifications.label: When the outlist-tracking gap is fixed, safe terminating propagation combined with fully-specified outlist semantics should yield complete incremental consistency — making recompute_all a verification tool rather than a correctness requirement

indefinite-self-correction-is-fully-audi.text: The system's indefinitely sustainable self-correction produces a fully auditable history without temporal degradation: every self-correction, maintenance action, and belief revision throughout the system's unbounded operational lifetime is traceable through nogoods, retraction records, and staleness metadata — auditability scales with time rather than decaying.

justifications.label: Connects the depth-7 leaf (indefinite sustainability) with depth-11 auditability — establishes that auditability is not merely a snapshot property but extends across unbounded operation, because both self-correction and its audit trail are sustained by the same minimality fixed-point

information-boundaries-are-controlled-at.text: The system controls information flow at every boundary: internally through access-tag authorization gating and token-budget constraints on output, and externally through bidirectional bounds on LLM input/output quality and defensive belief ingestion pipelines

justifications.label: Internal authorization-and-budget controls combined with external surface controls yield fully-controlled information boundaries

information-flow-is-authorization-and-bu.text: Information flow from the belief network is controlled along two independent dimensions: access tags gate which beliefs are visible to each caller (authorization control via transitive subset checks), while token budgets constrain how much of the visible network is emitted (volume control via priority-ordered truncation).

justifications.label: Authorization and budget controls independently constrain what flows out and how much

information-flow-is-controlled-in-both-d.text: Information flow is controlled at every system boundary: inbound data passes through production-hardened LLM integration (bounded execution, fail-soft handling, process isolation) and boundary-controlled information isolation (access tags, namespace partitioning), while outbound data is deterministic, authorized via transitive subset-gated access control, and budget-constrained — no uncontrolled data enters or leaves the belief network

justifications.label: Input hardening (depth-6) and output authorization (depth-4) are independently necessary but insufficient — bidirectional control means the system is a closed information boundary where every crossing is mediated, whether data flows in through LLM derivation and agent import or out through compact, search, and explain

information-governance-is-end-to-end-aut.text: Information governance is enforced end-to-end from pipeline-level resource management through output-level authorization: the pipeline is resource-governed through accurate bidirectional token budgets and access-controlled through transitive subset-gated tags, while the output layer adds deterministic authorized distillation through pure functions with fixed priority ordering — ensuring governance is not concentrated at a single chokepoint but layered across the complete information flow.

justifications.label: Pipeline-level governance and output-level authorization are complementary layers that prevent governance bypass through either channel

information-output-is-authorized-budgete.text: Information leaving the belief network is controlled along three independent dimensions: authorization gating ensures callers see only beliefs their tags permit, token budgets constrain output quantity, and the compact module's pure-function deterministic priority ordering guarantees reproducible distillation — output is simultaneously access-controlled, size-bounded, and predictable.

justifications.label: Authorization-and-budget control combined with deterministic bounded distillation provides triple-controlled information output

information-pipeline-is-resource-governe.text: The complete information pipeline is governed along two orthogonal axes: token budgets accurately constrain both input (proportional derive allocation) and output (compact distillation with budget enforcement), while access tags enforce transitive subset-based authorization at every read boundary — every piece of information is simultaneously resource-bounded and access-controlled.

justifications.label: Resource governance (depth-2) and access control (depth-1) are independent enforcement dimensions that together fully characterize information flow governance

init-db-raises-on-reinit-unless-force.text: `api.init_db()` raises `FileExistsError` when called on an existing database path unless `force=True` is passed, which overwrites.

init-db-refuses-existing-without-force.text: `api.init_db()` raises `FileExistsError` when the database file already exists, unless `force=True` is passed to allow overwrite.

init-has-zero-external-deps.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py` imports only `dataclasses` from the standard library, making it the dependency-free root of the package — imported by 29 test files and transitively by every module in `reasons_lib`.

init-is-pure-data-model.text: `reasons_lib/__init__.py` contains only dataclass definitions (`Node`, `Justification`, `Nogood`) with no behavior, validation, or I/O; it imports nothing from the project and sits at the bottom of the import graph.

init-requires-force-flag-for-reinitializ.text: Running `init` on an existing database without `--force` fails with exit code 1 and mentions `--force` in stderr, preventing accidental data loss from re-initialization.

initialization-and-reconciliation-conver.text: Both initialization paths (stored-state bootstrap trusting persisted values, and deterministic reasoning computing from scratch) and reconciliation operations (dual import/sync modes with heterogeneous truth state handling) converge to equivalent correct belief states — the system reaches the same outcome regardless of how or when beliefs enter the network.

justifications.label: Path-independent initialization combined with complete reconciliation ensures convergent ingestion

initialization-is-path-independent.text: Whether beliefs enter through stored-state bootstrap (load trusts stored truth values, import builds nodes before recompute_all) or through the deterministic reasoning engine (uniform pure evaluation with guaranteed termination), the system reaches correct truth states — bootstrap trusts values that were originally computed by the same deterministic engine, and import re-derives them via recompute_all, establishing path independence of initialization.

justifications.label: bootstrap trusts values computed by deterministic engine; import re-derives via same engine

initialization-is-pure-across-path-and-b.text: System initialization is a pure function of input data: convergence equivalence (all initialization paths yield identical state) composed with backend independence (path independence holds across SQLite and PostgreSQL) yields full initialization purity

justifications.label: Convergence equivalence eliminates path-dependence (stored-state bootstrap ≡ deterministic reasoning); backend independence eliminates substrate-dependence (SQLite ≡ PostgreSQL). The composition of two independent orthogonality axes (path × backend) yields a single purity guarantee: the resulting network state is a pure function of the input data, independent of both the implementation route taken and the storage substrate used.

initialization-is-safe-and-path-independ.text: System initialization produces identical belief states regardless of both initialization path (stored-state bootstrap vs deterministic reasoning) and storage backend (SQLite vs PostgreSQL providing equivalent safety through backend-appropriate mechanisms), eliminating all bootstrap-time variation

justifications.label: Path independence and backend agnosticism jointly eliminate all initialization-time environmental variation

initialization-is-safe-and-path-independ.text: System initialization reaches correct truth states regardless of the initialization path (stored-state bootstrap or deterministic reasoning), as bootstrap trusts values originally computed by the same deterministic engine and import re-derives them via recompute_all, supporting path independence of initialization; safety is enforced uniformly across architectural layers and storage backends (SQLite and PostgreSQL) through backend-appropriate mechanisms, with no safety property depending on a specific backend or layer.

input-validation-is-comprehensive-at-all.text: Input validation is enforced at every system boundary through complementary mechanisms: typed exceptions (ValueError for duplicates, PermissionError for access violations) enforce API-level preconditions at the call boundary, while defense-in-depth reference validation (import normalization dropping unknown refs, nogood filtering skipping invalid nodes, hallucinated ID rejection) catches invalid node references at every data-acceptance boundary.

justifications.label: API-level validation (depth-1) gates the call boundary; reference validation (depth-1) gates all data boundaries — no invalid input survives to reach the TMS engine regardless of entry point.

inspection-outputs-are-uniformly-normali.text: Both inspection mechanisms — belief review and staleness checking — produce normalized, schema-consistent, fail-safe output with deterministic structure suitable for automated consumption.

justifications.label: Review (6-key normalized schema, defaults to passing) and staleness (6-key uniform schema, sorted by node_id) both guarantee machine-parseable deterministic output

inspection-to-repair-enforces-read-mutat.text: The self-correction pipeline enforces strict phase separation: all diagnostic phases (review, check-stale) are purely read-only with zero mutation, and the sole mutation phase (repair) preserves existing outlist governance, ensuring no pipeline stage can silently corrupt network state or bypass established controls.

justifications.label: The separation claim requires both read-only diagnostics AND mutation-with-preservation; removing any one breaks the strict three-phase invariant (observe → observe → guarded-mutate).

integrity-and-scalability-are-complement.text: The system achieves comprehensive integrity (unified across all internal mutations and external belief ingestion) and sound multi-agent scalability (isolated namespaces, minimal primitives, deterministic propagation) simultaneously — these properties reinforce rather than trade off against each other because both derive from the same uniform evaluation rules.

justifications.label: Unifying the integrity story (depth-5) with the scalability story (depth-5) shows these are complementary consequences of uniform primitives, not competing design goals

integrity-enforced-across-architecture-a.text: Integrity is enforced along two orthogonal dimensions: vertically across architectural layers (clean data-model/TMS/persistence boundaries with snapshot persistence and CI gating) and horizontally across node lifecycle states (staleness checking skips OUT nodes without mutating, propagation skips retracted nodes while preserving them for restoration).

justifications.label: Architectural-layer integrity prevents cross-cutting mutations while lifecycle-state integrity prevents operating on nodes in inappropriate states — both dimensions must hold for system-wide consistency

integrity-is-an-emergent-consequence-of-.text: End-to-end integrity across all mutation paths and architectural boundaries is not an independently-achieved property requiring separate enforcement — it falls out of minimality as another emergent consequence, because uniform primitive evaluation leaves no gaps for inconsistency to enter.

justifications.label: if minimality generates all properties and the unified system has integrity, then integrity is itself a generated property rather than an imposed constraint

integrity-is-boundary-and-source-agnosti.text: System integrity is enforced agnostically along two independent dimensions — across the internal/external boundary (local mutations vs. external ingestion) and across mutation sources (human dialectics, LLM derivation, agent import) — because the same atomic-deterministic pipeline processes all combinations without branching on origin or direction.

justifications.label: Unifies the internal/external integrity boundary dimension with the mutation-source safety dimension to show integrity enforcement is fully agnostic to both boundary crossing and belief origin

internal-and-external-integrity-are-unif.text: Every operation — internal mutations (atomic transactions, deterministic propagation) and external belief ingestion (defensive validation, environment isolation, agent containment) — maintains end-to-end integrity through complementary safety mechanisms.

justifications.label: depth-5 — internal operational integrity and external belief bounding are independent safety dimensions that together cover all mutation sources

intra-cluster-focus-is-round-robin.text: `cluster_beliefs_intra` concentrates the entire budget on a single cluster selected by `sorted_clusters[round_num % k]` (largest-first), meaning successive derive rounds cycle through clusters in deterministic round-robin order rather than always focusing on the largest.

invariant-preservation-is-architecturall.text: The complete reasoning-and-revision architecture preserves invariants through minimal foundations not in a vacuum but atop concrete architectural safety — three-layer containment and atomic mutations provide the structural substrate within which minimal invariant preservation operates.

justifications.label: The logical property (invariant preservation through minimality, depth-6) and the physical substrate (three-layer boundaries + atomic mutations, depth-3) come from independent antecedent chains; their conjunction grounds the abstract in the concrete

invariant-preservation-is-comprehensive.text: System invariants are comprehensively preserved through two complementary mechanisms: the closed revision/lifecycle loop ensures temporal coverage across forward computation and backward revision, while dual structural/dynamic enforcement provides orthogonal protection through architectural grounding and minimality-enforced self-correction.

justifications.label: Temporal invariant coverage from the closed loop combines with structural/dynamic enforcement for multi-mechanism comprehensive protection

invariant-preservation-is-self-sustainin.text: Comprehensive invariant preservation — spanning revision loops, lifecycle management, and architectural grounding — is itself sustained by minimality's fixed-point property: the minimal primitives that preserve invariants are themselves invariants of the system, closing a meta-level consistency loop.

justifications.label: Minimality's fixed-point property applies reflexively to invariant preservation itself

invariant-preservation-is-total.text: Invariant preservation is both comprehensive in scope (spanning revision loops, lifecycle management, and structural/dynamic enforcement) and grounded across all independent dimensions (origin, time, and structure), achieving total invariant coverage with no gaps in either what is preserved or where preservation holds.

justifications.label: Comprehensive scope (the "what" of preservation) combined with multi-dimensional grounding (the "where/when" of preservation) yields total coverage; these address orthogonal aspects — mechanism vs. dimensions.

invariant-preservation-is-total-and-self.text: Invariant preservation is simultaneously total in scope (spanning all invariant dimensions and encompassing all belief types including externally-integrated ones) and self-sustaining in mechanism (maintained by minimality's fixed-point that dynamically corrects any departure) — comprehensiveness and sustainability are co-achieved rather than traded off.

justifications.label: Cross-connects two parallel depth-11 branches that independently established totality and self-sustainability of invariant preservation — neither is an antecedent of the other, yet they describe complementary aspects of the same system property

invariants-are-origin-time-and-structura.text: System invariants are anchored along three dimensions: they hold across all belief origins and through time (comprehensive scope), and they are grounded in the concrete architecture's clean layer boundaries and atomic operations (structural foundation) — the invariants are both broad in what they cover and deep in how they are enforced.

justifications.label: Origin-time coverage and architectural grounding converge to establish invariants with both comprehensive scope and structural foundation

invariants-are-structurally-and-dynamica.text: System invariants are preserved through two complementary layers: architectural grounding provides structural enforcement via clean layer boundaries and atomic mutations, while minimality-enforced self-correction actively detects and resolves violations through contradiction resolution and staleness detection.

justifications.label: static architectural structure and dynamic minimality-enforced correction jointly prevent invariant violations from persisting

invariants-hold-across-origin-and-time.text: System invariants hold along every independent dimension: across all belief origins (human-initiated, LLM-derived, agent-imported) via shared minimal foundations, and across both temporal phases (creation-time edge-case handling and maintenance-time staleness detection) including all semantic edge cases.

justifications.label: origin-spanning invariants plus temporal-spanning edge-case safety cover the full correctness matrix

invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing.text: `_invoke_claude()` raises `FileNotFoundError` if the `claude` CLI is not on `PATH`, rather than returning an error string — this is the one exception that `ask()` does not catch internally.

invoke-model-always-returns-string-or-ra.text: `invoke_model()` in `reasons/llm.py` always returns a `str` on success and raises an exception on failure — it never returns `None`, a list, or a raw dict.

invoke-model-return-contract-is-str-or-r.text: `invoke_model()` in `reasons/llm.py` always returns a `str` (the model's text response) or raises an exception; it never returns `None`, a dict, or a LangChain object — a contract relied upon by 15+ caller modules.

invoke-model-strips-claudecode-env.text: invoke_model() in llm.py strips the CLAUDECODE environment variable before all subprocess.run() calls, preventing recursive Claude Code entry from any module that uses the shared LLM interface (ask, derive, review).

issue-121-evolution-tolerance-audit.text: Issue #121: Audit evolution tolerance at all system boundaries — not all boundaries have documented forward-compatibility mechanisms

issue-122-review-fault-tolerance-audit.text: Issue #122: Audit review module for unhandled failure modes — three specific handlers do not establish coverage of all failure modes

issue-123-resource-footprint-audit.text: Issue #123: Audit resource footprint across all lifecycle phases — only deployment and startup phases are currently evidenced

issue-126-reference-validation-audit.text: Issue #126: Audit all node ID reference boundaries for validation — three specific boundaries do not establish coverage of every boundary

jaccard-tokenizer-splits-on-hyphens-and-.text: `_tokenize_id` splits belief IDs on hyphens and colons into token sets for Jaccard similarity comparison, so `foo-bar-baz` and `foo-bar-qux` share 2/4 tokens (0.5 similarity)

justification-addition-is-robust-across-.text: Adding a justification to an existing node achieves fully consistent multi-dimensional propagation — truth values, dependents index, and access tags — even when the dependency graph contains dangling references or lifecycle-marked nodes, because propagation safely handles both graph anomalies and node lifecycle states.

justifications.label: Consistent justification propagation combined with graph-inconsistency safety ensures robust state transitions regardless of graph quality

justification-evaluation-is-context-inde.text: Justification evaluation produces identical results regardless of evaluation context: it is pure (no side effects), uniform across types (SL/CP use the same validity rule), and temporally invariant (attaching a justification at creation or later yields the same truth outcome) — making truth computation fully context-free

justifications.label: Purity and type-uniformity (depth-1) combined with temporal invariance (depth-1) yields complete context-independence — evaluation depends only on antecedent/outlist truth values, never on when, how, or in what order justifications were attached

justification-evaluation-is-uniform-and-.text: All justification types (SL and CP) use the same validity rule (antecedents IN, outlist OUT), evaluated as a pure function with no side effects

justifications.label: Uniform evaluation means the TMS engine has exactly one truth-computation path regardless of justification type

justification-order-preserved-via-rowid.text: Justification insertion order is preserved across save/load cycles using `AUTOINCREMENT` rowid and `ORDER BY rowid` on read, which matters because justification priority affects truth maintenance.

justification-review-defaults-to-all.text: `parse_justification_review` defaults the `classification` field to `"ALL"` (the conservative choice requiring all antecedents) when the LLM omits or nulls it, and normalizes all values to uppercase (`"any"` → `"ANY"`).

justification-review-eligibility-require.text: Only nodes with at least one SL-type justification whose antecedent list length is ≥ `min_antecedents` (default 2) are sent to the model; premises (no justifications) and single-antecedent derived nodes are always excluded.

justification-review-is-read-only.text: `api.review_justifications` is strictly read-only: it must not mutate stored justifications, and tests explicitly re-read nodes after the call to assert the original SL antecedent lists are unchanged.

justification-timing-is-irrelevant-to-ev.text: Justification evaluation produces identical truth semantics regardless of when a justification is attached: add_node evaluates justifications immediately at insertion, and add_justification triggers identical propagation when attached post-creation — the system has no time-of-attachment sensitivity.

justifications.label: Both entry points use the same pure evaluation function, eliminating time-of-attachment sensitivity

justification-valid-is-pure.text: `_justification_valid` is a pure query with no side effects, no logging, and no mutations to network state

justification-validity-requires-inlist-i.text: A justification is valid iff all antecedents are IN and all outlist nodes are OUT; this single rule drives retraction cascades, kill-switch behavior, challenges, and supersession

kill-switch-cascade-is-reversible.text: Retracting `agent:active` cascades all agent beliefs to OUT via the inactive relay flipping IN; re-asserting `agent:active` reverses the cascade, restoring all beliefs to IN via the same BFS propagation

kill-switch-uses-outlist-not-antecedent.text: The `agent:inactive` node is placed in each imported belief's outlist (not antecedents) so that retracting `agent:active` cascades all imported beliefs to OUT, while per-belief retraction still works independently

knowledge-equilibria-are-correction-conv.text: Knowledge growth converges to negation-transparent equilibria with complete propagation fidelity, where every correction that shapes that convergence operates on accurate topology — dependency completeness ensures corrections propagate through the true graph structure, not an approximation.

justifications.label: Knowledge equilibria transparency combined with topological accuracy of the corrections driving convergence

knowledge-equilibria-are-fully-character.text: Knowledge revision converges to equilibria that are simultaneously self-sustaining through minimality's fixed-point, invariant-preserving across all belief types, correction-convergent with complete dispute resolution fidelity, and topology-accurate with verified dependency propagation — the complete set of equilibrium properties.

justifications.label: Combines the two independent equilibrium characterizations — self-sustaining invariant preservation and correction-convergent topology accuracy — into a fully characterized equilibrium

knowledge-equilibria-are-invariant-prese.text: Knowledge growth converges to negation-transparent equilibria with complete propagation fidelity where all system invariants are simultaneously total in scope and self-sustaining through minimality — the system can grow its knowledge base indefinitely while every invariant remains actively maintained.

justifications.label: Convergent transparent equilibria establish the state the system reaches; total self-sustaining invariant preservation ensures that state is fully trustworthy along every invariant dimension

knowledge-expansion-is-exhaustive-within.text: Exhaustive knowledge expansion — deterministic reversible reasoning combined with complete LLM-driven derivation with guaranteed termination — is achieved through production-hardened LLM integration operating within controlled information boundaries, ensuring the system discovers all derivable conclusions while maintaining robustness guarantees at every stage of the pipeline.

justifications.label: Connects exhaustive expansion (what the system achieves) with hardened integration (how it achieves it safely) — expansion is not just bounded but production-grade

knowledge-growth-is-convergent-assured-a.text: The system's knowledge base growth achieves three simultaneous guarantees: deterministic convergence with topology preservation (every modification reaches a stable state), universal multidimensional assurance (temporal, reliability, and control dimensions all covered), and indefinite self-correction (resource-sustainable correction sustains the growth lifecycle without temporal bound) — enabling autonomous long-running operation.

justifications.label: Convergent growth establishes that the system reaches correct states; indefinite self-correction establishes that it maintains them — together enabling autonomous operation

knowledge-growth-is-exhaustive-and-infor.text: Exhaustive knowledge expansion — deterministic reversible reasoning combined with complete LLM-driven derivation with guaranteed termination within hardened integration boundaries — operates under comprehensive bidirectional information governance: inbound data passes through production-hardened LLM integration with process isolation and fail-soft semantics, while outbound information is constrained by access-tag authorization and token-budget limits.

justifications.label: Exhaustive expansion maximizes knowledge discovery, while bidirectional information governance ensures this expansion respects both input safety and output confidentiality — growth is not unconstrained but operates within a fully controlled information envelope.

knowledge-growth-reaches-transparent-equ.text: The system's knowledge growth converges to equilibria that are simultaneously negation-transparent (the final stable state is uniquely determined by evaluation order-invariant rules over negative semantics) and propagation-complete (every truth change cascades to every transitively dependent node), with indefinite self-correction ensuring these equilibrium properties are maintained across unbounded operational time

justifications.label: Growth convergence (depth-11) and equilibrium quality (depth-9) are unified — the system not only grows indefinitely but the states it converges to have independently-established transparency and fidelity guarantees

knowledge-revision-converges-to-self-sus.text: Knowledge revision — evaluation-invariant, auditable across all origins, and indefinitely self-correcting — converges to equilibria that are simultaneously invariant-preserving and self-sustaining through minimality's fixed-point property, forming a closed loop where revision quality and equilibrium stability mutually reinforce.

justifications.label: Indefinite self-correcting revision (depth-9) feeds into invariant-preserving self-sustaining equilibria (depth-13) — the revision process and its convergence target are jointly stable

knowledge-revision-is-invariant-and-inde.text: The system's knowledge revision achieves two independent perpetuity guarantees: evaluation invariance (revision governs richer state than truth values while preserving identical evaluation semantics regardless of revision path) across all belief origins, and indefinite self-correction through sustainable growth mechanisms that never exhaust system resources

justifications.label: Evaluation-invariant revision (depth-8) and indefinitely sustainable growth (depth-8) are independent — together they guarantee that knowledge can grow forever without revision producing inconsistent evaluations

langfuse-handler-is-process-singleton.text: `_get_langfuse_handler()` creates the Langfuse tracing callback at most once per process (lazy singleton) and returns `None` when `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` is unset.

legacy-import-neither-crashes-nor-clobbe.text: Importing a file without metadata (legacy JSON without `"meta"`, Markdown without frontmatter) succeeds with defaults and does not destroy existing metadata in the target database — both crash-safety and data-preservation are guaranteed.

lifecycle-awareness-spans-checking-and-p.text: Both read-only inspection and mutation-driven propagation respect node lifecycle consistently: staleness checking skips OUT nodes and never mutates state, while propagation skips retracted nodes and preserves trigger identity — lifecycle state is honored across the system regardless of whether the operation is read or write.

justifications.label: depth-2 — read path (staleness) and write path (propagation) independently enforce lifecycle awareness, suggesting a system-wide invariant

lifecycle-governance-achieves-gap-free-s.text: Metadata-enabled lifecycle governance with deterministic source integrity and exception-safe recoverability achieves truly gap-free source coverage — every source file is verified, every lifecycle decision is grounded in verifiable source state, and no silent source gap undermines governance decisions about staleness or retraction.

justifications.label: Combined lifecycle governance properties establish determinism and exception safety independently; gap-free coverage additionally requires that missing source files are not silently ignored

lifecycle-governance-achieves-gap-free-s.text: Metadata-enabled lifecycle governance with deterministic source integrity and exception-safe recoverability supports robust source coverage — source files are verified through collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing within clean three-layer boundaries, lifecycle decisions about staleness and belief currency rest on verifiable source state, and exception-safe recoverable revision mechanics mitigate the risk of silent source gaps undermining those governance decisions.

lifecycle-governance-has-deterministic-s.text: Metadata-enabled lifecycle governance is backed by deterministic, architecturally-grounded source integrity — lifecycle decisions about staleness and belief currency rest on collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing within clean three-layer boundaries, ensuring that the source-grounding of lifecycle governance is itself structurally sound and deterministic.

justifications.label: Lifecycle governance depends on source integrity; source integrity is independently shown to be deterministic and architecturally grounded — so lifecycle governance inherits a verified foundation

lifecycle-governance-is-exception-safe-a.text: Metadata-enabled source-grounded lifecycle governance is backed by exception-safe recoverable revision mechanics — lifecycle decisions about staleness and source integrity are protected by the same exception handling that safeguards contradiction resolution and dialectical transformation.

justifications.label: Independent lifecycle governance (metadata + source verification) and revision safety (exception handling + recovery) compose into a system where source-grounded lifecycle decisions are fault-tolerant

lifecycle-governance-is-metadata-enabled.text: Rich lifecycle governance — extending beyond binary IN/OUT truth through extensible metadata carrying retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, and challenges — is concretely grounded in fail-safe source integrity: the source pipeline (convention-based resolution, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing, comprehensive staleness detection) populates and verifies the metadata state that enables lifecycle governance, closing the loop between abstract lifecycle management and concrete source verification.

justifications.label: Metadata enables rich governance and the source pipeline grounds that governance in verifiable reality

lifecycle-is-deterministic-and-architect.text: Gapless lifecycle management is doubly reinforced: deterministic reasoning ensures predictable state trajectories with full monitoring, while architectural safety provides the structural foundation through clean layer boundaries and atomic mutations.

justifications.label: Two independent foundations for lifecycle robustness converge — determinism from reasoning engine, structure from architecture

lifecycle-is-deterministic-grounded-and-.text: Gapless lifecycle management is triply reinforced: deterministic reasoning ensures predictable state trajectories, architectural grounding provides structural enforcement via clean layer boundaries, and the underlying architecture is verified free of hidden fragilities — eliminating both behavioral unpredictability and structural failure modes simultaneously.

justifications.label: Deterministic prediction (behavioral soundness) and structural soundness (no hidden fragility) are independently established; their conjunction eliminates both failure mode categories for lifecycle management.

lifecycle-management-is-gapless.text: The system manages belief lifecycle without gaps across all operation types: staleness checking detects all forms of source drift, propagation respects node lifecycle states, and both read and write paths enforce consistent lifecycle semantics — no operation ignores or corrupts lifecycle state.

justifications.label: drift detection + lifecycle-aware propagation = complete lifecycle management (depth-3 GATE from two depth-2)

lifecycle-operates-on-unfragile-architec.text: Gapless lifecycle management — spanning staleness detection, propagation lifecycle awareness, and import reconciliation — operates on an architecture verified to have no hidden fragility points, ensuring lifecycle operations cannot be undermined by latent structural weaknesses in the central dependency or layer boundaries.

justifications.label: Lifecycle robustness is grounded in verified absence of architectural fragility

linkify-is-idempotent.text: `_linkify` in `build_wiki.py` skips node IDs already embedded in `[id](...)` Markdown link syntax, so running the function multiple times on the same content produces no duplicate or nested links.

list-clusters-guarantees-complete-partit.text: `list_clusters` returns a complete partition of the input: every belief ID provided as input appears in exactly one cluster across the full result, with no belief duplicated or omitted.

list-clusters-partitions-all-beliefs.text: `list_clusters` assigns every input belief to exactly one cluster with no drops or duplicates — the union of all cluster members equals the input set.

list-negative-batches-at-40.text: `api.list_negative` splits candidates into batches of 40, so 120 keyword-matching nodes produce exactly 3 LLM calls.

list-negative-batches-at-50.text: `list_negative` splits candidate nodes into batches of approximately 50 for LLM classification, verified by the test suite asserting exactly 3 LLM calls for 120 candidates.

list-negative-is-bounded-and-batch-scala.text: The list-negative classification pipeline is both defensively bounded (two-stage keyword + LLM filtering with hallucination rejection and graceful malformed-output handling) and scalably partitioned (fixed batch size of ~50 candidates per LLM call), ensuring predictable resource usage and bounded LLM costs regardless of belief network size.

justifications.label: Defensive bounding prevents quality degradation; fixed batching prevents resource exhaustion — together they make classification safe at any scale.

list-negative-is-defensively-bounded.text: The negative belief listing pipeline applies defense-in-depth: keyword pre-filtering narrows candidates before LLM classification, hallucinated node IDs are discarded against the actual network, and malformed LLM output falls back gracefully to zero count rather than raising.

justifications.label: Three independent defensive measures form a complete safety pipeline for LLM-driven negative classification

list-negative-json-parser-tolerates-pros.text: The `list_negative` LLM classification response parser uses `re.finditer` to extract JSON objects from responses that include prose preamble, handling the common LLM pattern of prefacing structured output with natural language rather than requiring clean JSON.

list-negative-parser-is-fully-resilient.text: The list-negative LLM response parser handles all degradation levels: regex extraction recovers JSON objects from prose-laden responses, and completely unparseable output returns zero results gracefully rather than raising exceptions.

justifications.label: Two independent parser robustness properties combine to cover the full failure spectrum from partial corruption to total garbling

list-negative-uses-two-stage-classificat.text: `list_negative` uses keyword pre-filtering against a hardcoded `NEGATIVE_TERMS` list (~50 words), then LLM classification via `ask._invoke_claude` to eliminate false positives.

list-nodes-defaults-source-type-to-empty.text: When a node has no `source_type` set, `api.list_nodes` returns `""` (an empty string, not None or a missing key) for the `source_type` field on that node's flat dict representation.

llm-belief-operations-span-creation-and-.text: All LLM-driven belief operations — creation via derive (with safety, completeness, and resource efficiency) and classification via list-negative (with defensive bounding and batch scaling) — share consistent defensive patterns across the complete belief quality lifecycle.

justifications.label: The derive and list-negative pipelines independently achieve defensive robustness; together they cover the full LLM-driven belief lifecycle from creation through classification with no quality gap

llm-belief-pipeline-is-fully-quality-enf.text: The system's complete LLM-driven belief pipeline — both generation (derive with safety, completeness, and coverage) and classification (list_negative with defensive bounding) — achieves fully code-enforced quality constraints at every stage, provided minimum-antecedent validation moves from prompt-only to code-enforced.

justifications.label: Full LLM belief pipeline quality requires code-enforced antecedent validation

llm-cost-summary-printed-to-stderr.text: Every LLM-invoking CLI handler follows a consistent three-step cost-tracking pattern: `reset_cost_tracker()` before the API call, then `format_cost_summary()` printed to `sys.stderr` (not stdout) after, keeping cost reporting separated from result output.

llm-dispatch-routes-by-model-string-pref.text: `invoke_model()` uses the model string prefix as the sole dispatch mechanism: strings without `api:`/`vertex:` go through CLI subprocess (claude, gemini, ollama), while `api:*` and `vertex:*` go through langchain SDK clients.

llm-driven-mutations-are-safely-bounded.text: LLM-driven belief derivation is safely bounded by defense in depth: the derive pipeline validates proposals with fail-soft filtering, Jaccard retraction guards, and environment stripping at the LLM boundary, while the API layer enforces atomic load/save with write-flag gating and dict-only returns at the persistence boundary — malformed or adversarial LLM output cannot corrupt the network.

justifications.label: LLM-boundary defenses (depth-1) + persistence-boundary atomicity (depth-1) form defense in depth against the unique risks of machine-generated mutations

llm-extra-excludes-openai.text: The `llm` meta-extra in pyproject.toml deliberately excludes `openai`; users requiring OpenAI must install `[llm,openai]` separately.

llm-fault-tolerance-is-multi-granular.text: LLM fault tolerance operates at two independent granularities: module-level fail-soft handling ensures entire operations degrade gracefully when the LLM is unavailable, while item-level batch fault isolation ensures individual failures within derive and review batches are contained without affecting other items in the same batch.

justifications.label: Two orphaned depth-1 beliefs capturing independent fault-isolation granularities that together provide defense-in-depth within the LLM pipeline

llm-integration-fails-softly-across-modu.text: All LLM-facing modules apply consistent fail-soft error handling: the ask module always returns a string even when the LLM is unavailable, and the derive pipeline accumulates per-proposal errors rather than raising exceptions — no LLM failure path crashes the system.

justifications.label: Cross-module consistency — both LLM integration points (ask and derive) apply fail-soft patterns, establishing a system-wide invariant for LLM error handling

llm-integration-is-bounded-fail-soft-and.text: LLM integration achieves three independent safety properties across all modules: execution bounds (iteration caps and timeouts), fail-soft error handling (always returns usable results on failure), and process isolation (subprocess invocation with CLAUDECODE environment stripping to prevent recursive entry)

justifications.label: Bounded fail-soft execution combined with subprocess isolation yields defense-in-depth for all LLM interactions

llm-integration-is-defense-in-depth-acro.text: All LLM integration achieves defense-in-depth across two independent layers: application-level defensive bounding provides iteration caps, fail-soft error handling, Jaccard retraction guards, and hallucination filtering across all LLM-facing operations, while infrastructure-level process isolation executes all LLM calls through subprocess boundaries with CLAUDECODE environment scrubbing to prevent recursive invocation — ensuring safety at both the semantic and process boundaries.

justifications.label: Application-layer defense and infrastructure-layer isolation are independent safety dimensions that combine into comprehensive defense-in-depth

llm-integration-is-production-hardened.text: LLM integration achieves production-grade robustness across all dimensions: infrastructure-level safety through bounded execution, fail-soft error handling, and process isolation prevents runaway or recursive invocations, while operational-level coverage and fault tolerance ensures both derive (batch) and ask (interactive) paths complete successfully or degrade gracefully under all failure modes.

justifications.label: Infrastructure-level safety (bounded/fail-soft/isolated) combined with operational-level coverage and fault tolerance produces production-hardened LLM integration

llm-invoke-checks-path-before-run.text: Covered by existing `invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing` (same behavior generalized to all model binaries).

llm-is-pluggable-enhancement-not-core-in.text: LLM capabilities (summarization in `compact.py`, derivation assistance in `llm.py`) are a pluggable enhancement layered on the TMS core; the core inference engine (`network.py`, `derive.py`, `repair.py`) has no dependency on any LLM module.

llm-mock-targets-subprocess-boundary.text: All LLM-dependent tests patch `reasons.llm.shutil.which` and `reasons.llm.subprocess.run` specifically, ensuring the text-parsing and type-matching logic in `classify_defeat_reason` always executes for real while only the external process invocation is replaced.

llm-mutations-are-bounded-end-to-end.text: LLM-driven belief derivation is bounded at every stage of the pipeline: input validation (fail-soft filtering, Jaccard retraction guard, environment isolation), atomic persistence (context-managed load/save), and output propagation (deterministic terminating BFS with lifecycle-aware traversal).

justifications.label: depth-3 — input bounding (derive pipeline defenses) and output bounding (propagation safety) are independently established, together covering the full mutation lifecycle

llm-prompt-always-via-stdin.text: Prompts are passed to LLM subprocesses via `subprocess.run(input=...)`, never as command-line arguments — avoiding shell injection and argument length limits.

llm-resolve-ollama-preserves-inner-colon.text: `resolve_model_cmd("ollama:model:tag")` splits on the first colon only, keeping `model:tag` intact as the Ollama model identifier.

llm-subprocess-invocation-is-security-ha.text: All LLM subprocess invocations follow a unified security pattern: CLAUDECODE env is stripped to prevent recursive invocation, and prompts are passed via stdin (never argv) to prevent shell-injection and argument parsing vulnerabilities.

justifications.label: Convergent evidence — each subprocess call site independently enforces the same two security properties (recursive-injection prevention + shell-injection prevention), establishing a project-wide invariant for LLM process spawning.

llm-subprocess-isolation-prevents-recurs.text: All LLM subprocess invocations strip the CLAUDECODE environment variable to prevent recursive Claude Code entry, enforced centrally in invoke_model() and inherited by all LLM-facing modules (ask, derive, review).

justifications.label: Centralized enforcement in invoke_model covers all LLM-facing modules

llm-subprocess-mock-requires-two-patches.text: Testing infrastructure detail (which objects to patch), not a production code invariant. The underlying fact about `shutil.which` + `subprocess.run` is already captured by `all-external-execution-is-subprocess-isolated` and `invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing`.

llm-thinking-strip-ollama-only.text: Thinking-marker stripping (`Thinking...` / `...done thinking.`) is applied only to Ollama model output; Claude and Gemini output passes through unmodified even if it contains the same markers.

llm-three-error-types.text: Too granular — the three error types (ValueError, FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError) are implementation details of the error taxonomy already captured by existing beliefs about fail-fast and fail-soft behavior.

loaded-network-supports-further-inferenc.text: A `Network` returned by `Storage.load()` is a fully operational inference engine (retract, restore, and propagation all work), not a frozen read-only snapshot — the storage layer must reconstruct all internal graph links including SL/justification connections.

maintenance-loop-is-fully-observable.text: The minimality-sustained closed maintenance loop has complete observability: every self-correction leaves traceable history (nogoods, retraction records, staleness reports), enabling full audit of how the system maintains itself over time.

justifications.label: closed-loop maintenance combined with traceable correction history yields full observability of all maintenance activity

make-nodes-excludes-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a claim about production code behavior

make-nodes-omits-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a production code invariant

mark-duplicate-and-superseded-reject-sel.text: Both `mark_duplicate(x, x)` and `mark_superseded(x, x)` raise `ValueError` with a message indicating self-reference is forbidden, leaving the node in its original `IN` truth state unchanged.

mark-duplicate-overwrites-prior-retract-.text: Calling `mark_duplicate` or `mark_superseded` on a node that is already `OUT` (from a prior retraction) succeeds and overwrites the existing `retract_reason` metadata with the dedup/supersession-specific message (e.g., `"Duplicate of <canonical>"`) rather than failing or appending.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout-60s.text: `call_tool()` blocks for up to 60 seconds per invocation via `future.result(timeout=60)`; if the MCP server hangs, the calling thread unblocks with `TimeoutError`.

mcp-bridge-command-is-shell-string.text: `McpBridge.__init__` expects a single shell command string (e.g. `"npx @mcp/server-fs /path"`) which is parsed via `shlex.split`; passing a list of arguments directly is not supported.

mcp-bridge-connect-blocks-up-to-30s.text: `connect()` blocks the calling thread for up to 30 seconds waiting for MCP session initialization via `_ready.wait(timeout=30)`, then raises `TimeoutError` if the server doesn't respond.

mcp-bridge-duck-type-interface.text: The ask module's MCP dispatch expects any bridge object to implement `list_tools() → list[dict]`, `get_instructions() → str`, and `call_tool(name, arguments) → str`; no concrete class import is required.

mcp-bridge-is-deliberately-stateless-and.text: The MCP bridge is architecturally committed to simplicity over resilience: it is a one-shot session with no retry or reconnection, its tool catalog is a frozen snapshot taken at connect time, and its interface is duck-typed (no formal protocol) — trading operational robustness for predictability and minimal coupling.

justifications.label: Convergent design philosophy — each property independently supports the "deliberately ephemeral" characterization; the conclusion holds as long as any one of these constraints is in force, since each individually precludes long-lived stateful integration.

mcp-bridge-is-one-shot-session.text: `McpBridge` has no retry logic, no reconnection, and no health-check; if the MCP server dies mid-session, the caller must create a new `McpBridge` instance and call `connect()` again.

mcp-bridge-is-timeout-bounded-at-all-pha.text: MCP bridge operations are timeout-bounded at both connection establishment (30s) and per-tool execution (60s), preventing indefinite blocking on unresponsive MCP servers at any lifecycle phase.

justifications.label: Connection and execution timeouts independently bound both MCP lifecycle phases

mcp-bridge-runs-dedicated-event-loop-thr.text: Each `McpBridge` instance runs its own asyncio event loop on a daemon thread; the MCP session stays alive until `close()` signals the shutdown event, bridging the sync/async boundary via `run_coroutine_threadsafe`.

mcp-bridge-tools-snapshot-at-connect.text: The tool catalog and server instructions are populated once during `connect()` and never refreshed — there is no mechanism to pick up tools added after the initial handshake.

mcp-db-discovery-precedence-env-then-cwd.text: `_find_db()` resolves the SQLite path with strict precedence: `REASONS_DB` environment variable, then walking up from `os.getcwd()`, then `api.DEFAULT_DB` — and `_get_db()` caches the result in the module-level `_db` attribute.

mcp-db-resolution-precedence.text: Database path resolution follows a strict order: `REASONS_DB` env var → walk up from `cwd` looking for `reasons.db` → `api.DEFAULT_DB`, with the result cached in a module-level `_db` singleton resolved at most once per process.

mcp-error-as-data-not-control-flow.text: Exceptions in MCP tool handlers are caught and serialized to `{"error": "..."}` JSON strings so the LLM receives a parseable recovery message; the MCP connection never dies from a tool exception.

mcp-falsy-to-none-idempotency.text: The MCP layer converts falsy sentinels (`0` for limit, `""` for optional string params like status/namespace) to `None` via `x or None` before calling `reasons.api` functions, which treat `None` as "no filter / no limit."

mcp-is-optional-dependency.text: The `mcp` package is guarded by try/except at import time; `_require_mcp()` defers the `ImportError` to `McpBridge` construction so the module can be imported unconditionally without the SDK installed.

mcp-read-only-tools-lack-error-wrapping.text: The read-only tools (`compact`, `search`, `list_beliefs`, `status`, `list_gated`, `export_markdown`, `topics`) have no try/except wrapper, so any `api` exception propagates as a raw MCP protocol-level error rather than a structured `{"error": "..."}` JSON response.

mcp-server-is-zero-logic-facade.text: `reasons/mcp_server.py` contains zero domain logic; every tool body is a one-or-two-line delegation into `reasons/api.*` with a try/except wrapper, and the module owns only wire-protocol serialization and DB path discovery.

mcp-server-stdio-purity-contract.text: The MCP server process must not emit anything to stdout other than JSON-RPC frames; any `print()` or stray output would corrupt the stdio transport and break the client, so `main()` and all tool handlers must avoid writing to stdout.

mcp-tool-json-renders-no-trailing-comma.text: When a MCP tool has zero parameters, `_build_tools_section` renders the JSON example as `'{"tool": "name"}'` (no trailing comma), preventing LLM JSON-parser failures.

mcp-tools-never-raise-return-error-json.text: Every MCP tool function in `reasons/mcp_server.py` catches internal exceptions and returns a JSON string containing `{"error": "<message>"}` rather than raising — the protocol contract is "JSON-or-text, never an exception."

mcp-tools-return-strings-only.text: All MCP tool handlers in `reasons/mcp_server.py` return `str` (JSON-dumped or markdown); no structured type crosses the MCP boundary, a requirement of the `FastMCP` tool contract.

merkle-antecedents-sorted-for-determinis.text: In `_fresh_content_hash`, antecedent Merkle hashes are collected and `sorted(...)` before concatenation, guaranteeing the content hash is identical regardless of the order antecedents appear in the justification's list.

merkle-backfill-is-lossless.text: After `backfill_hashes()` fills empty `text_hash`/`content_hash` fields, a subsequent `check_integrity()` reports zero missing hashes and zero mutations — the backfill operation is idempotent and produces a clean graph.

merkle-cycle-produces-empty-string-hash.text: A cyclic justification chain does not raise or loop infinitely; `_fresh_merkle_hash` detects the cycle via the `visiting` set and returns `sha256("")` (hash of empty string), silently weakening the integrity guarantee without crashing.

merkle-fresh-computation-is-non-circular.text: The `_fresh_merkle_hash` and `_fresh_content_hash` functions compute hashes exclusively from `node.text` and network topology; they never read `node.text_hash` or `justification.content_hash` from the network, ensuring verification compares a freshly-derived value against the stored one.

merkle-hash-follows-single-justification.text: The Merkle hash for a node incorporates only its `supporting_justification` and that justification's antecedents recursively; other justifications on the same node do not affect the computed hash, making the integrity guarantee per-path rather than per-node.

merkle-module-is-stdlib-only.text: `reasons/merkle.py` imports only `hashlib` from the standard library with zero third-party or intra-package dependencies, enabling isolated unit testing and reuse without pulling in the full network stack.

merkle-mutation-detection-is-transitive-.text: A single leaf-node text mutation cascades up the DAG: `check_integrity` flags all transitive ancestors (not just direct dependents) as chain mutations, because each ancestor's `content_hash` incorporates its child's hash.

merkle-verification-never-raises.text: `verify_node`, `verify_justification`, and `verify_all` never raise exceptions; they return `None` (clean) or a structured finding dict with a `"type"` discriminator (`"text_mutation"` or `"chain_mutation"`), making all integrity issues data rather than control flow.

metadata-actively-governs-truth-propagat.text: Lifecycle state carried in node metadata (retraction flags, stale reasons) is not passive storage but actively governs truth propagation behavior — retracted nodes are skipped during BFS traversal and trigger nodes are never recomputed — ensuring that the universal extension mechanism directly controls truth maintenance rather than merely recording state

justifications.label: Metadata extensibility means any lifecycle concern can be expressed as a metadata key, and propagation's lifecycle awareness means that metadata directly influences truth computation — the combination closes the loop between state representation and state enforcement

metadata-created-at-preservation-contrac.text: If the caller passes a non-empty `created_at` string, it is preserved verbatim as the original creation timestamp; if empty or `None`, current UTC time is used. `updated_at` is always current UTC regardless of caller input, so the two diverge on re-export.

metadata-enables-lifecycle-governance-be.text: Node metadata enables lifecycle governance capabilities that transcend the binary IN/OUT truth model: extensible metadata provides structured lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, supersession markers) that actively governs both read and write paths, while staleness information is preserved and surfaced in compact output despite having no dedicated truth state in the TMS data model.

justifications.label: Metadata governance (depth-4) and staleness surfacing (depth-3) together show metadata compensates for the binary truth model's expressiveness limitations

metadata-generator-degrades-to-unknown.text: `_get_generator()` wraps `importlib.metadata.version("ftl-reasons")` in a `try/except Exception`; any failure (including `PackageNotFoundError`) results in `"ftl-reasons/unknown"` rather than raising, ensuring metadata stamping never blocks an export.

metadata-governance-flows-through-safe-t.text: Metadata-carried lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags) actively governs truth propagation that is itself topology-complete and inconsistency-safe — lifecycle decisions propagate through all transitive dependencies including outlist-connected paths, even in the presence of dangling references, without runtime errors.

justifications.label: Active metadata governance combined with inconsistency-safe topology-complete propagation

metadata-governance-has-topology-complet.text: The rich lifecycle state carried in metadata — retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags — participates in topology-complete robust propagation that reaches all transitively dependent nodes under all graph conditions, ensuring lifecycle governance decisions cascade completely through the network rather than stopping at direct dependents.

justifications.label: Metadata governance and topology-complete propagation are independently established; combining shows lifecycle decisions (retraction pins, access tag inheritance, staleness) cascade completely and robustly through the full dependency graph

metadata-governed-modifications-are-bidi.text: Bidirectional belief modifications — contradiction resolution and defeat reversal — propagate metadata-governed lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags) topology-completely within a deterministic lifecycle, ensuring every modification in either direction carries complete metadata through the entire dependency graph with no governance gap between forward and backward changes.

justifications.label: Both beliefs share topology-complete propagation within deterministic lifecycle; combining reveals bidirectional modifications are fully metadata-governed

metadata-governs-lifecycle-across-read-a.text: Node lifecycle state carried in metadata actively governs both mutation behavior (retracted nodes skipped during truth propagation, sticky retraction surviving recompute) and inspection behavior (staleness checking skips OUT nodes, compact surfaces stale reasons) — a single metadata mechanism controls the system's complete operational surface.

justifications.label: Write-path governance (depth-2) and read-path governance (depth-2) share the same metadata fields, making lifecycle a unified cross-cutting concern rather than two independent implementations.

metadata-is-single-source-of-truth-for-e.text: Six production modules (`api.py`, `cli.py`, `export_card.py`, `export_markdown.py`, `pg.py`, `storage.py`) all call `build_meta()` rather than constructing the metadata dict inline, centralizing the schema to prevent field-name drift across export formats.

metadata-is-universal-extension-mechanis.text: Node metadata is the universal extension mechanism carrying all structured lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, challenges, access tags, supersession markers), and retraction flags pinned in metadata survive recomputation to enforce sticky retraction.

justifications.label: Metadata carries structured state AND survives recomputation — it is both the carrier and the enforcer of lifecycle semantics

metadata-module-is-formatter-not-validat.text: `build_meta()` contains no `raise` statements and performs no input validation; passing `node_count=-1`, `project_name=None`, or a non-ISO `created_at` string will not trigger an error — input correctness is the caller's responsibility.

metadata-provides-extensible-lifecycle-g.text: Node metadata is simultaneously the universal extension mechanism for network state (carrying all structured lifecycle properties with consistent audit tracking) and the active governor of truth propagation behavior across both read and write paths — retracted and stale nodes are skipped in propagation and staleness checking respectively, driven by the same metadata fields.

justifications.label: Metadata is not merely storage — it both defines extensible state and actively constrains system behavior, making it the unifying mechanism for state management and lifecycle governance.

migrated-retraction-all-identification-i.text: review-beliefs: "Collision-free" is strictly stronger than the "consistent, referenceable identification" established by the antecedents — addressability does not imply collision prevention across identifier spaces. migrated-retraction-all-llm-interactions.text: review-beliefs: The claim attributes environment isolation to both paths, but only the derive antecedent mentions it; additionally "All LLM-facing operations" is overclaimed when review and list-negative modules are unaddressed.
