tag-inheritance-is-transitive-union.text: Derived nodes inherit the sorted union of all ancestor `access_tags`, propagating transitively through arbitrarily long justification chains including diamond dependencies.

tag-propagation-is-dynamic.text: Adding a justification to an existing node triggers access tag recomputation that cascades through all downstream dependents via BFS, not just at node creation time.

tag-representation-and-api-boundary-tran.text: Internally, an untagged node has the `access_tags` key entirely absent from its metadata dict (not an empty list), making it visible to all callers; the `trace_access_tags` API translates this key-absence into an explicit `[]` return value at the public boundary.

test-network-covers-all-propagation-path.text: Test coverage claim, not a codebase invariant — what the test suite covers can change without affecting production behavior

test-suite-validates-shim-import-chain.text: 25+ test files import from `reasons_lib.*` rather than `reasons.*`, meaning the test suite exercises the shim's re-export chain and would not independently detect if a canonical module's `__all__` were misconfigured to exclude expected symbols.

tests-excluded-from-distribution.text: Only `reasons_lib/` is packaged for distribution; the `tests/` directory is excluded via explicit `[tool.setuptools] packages = ["reasons_lib"]` configuration.

tests-package-importability-required-by-.text: `tests/test_pg.py` resolves the `tests` package by name (`from tests import ...`), so the empty `tests/__init__.py` must exist for that import path to work correctly; deleting it makes the import fragile or broken.

tests-verify-via-output-headers.text: Test methodology detail (how assertions parse output), not a codebase architectural invariant

text-hash-is-sha256-of-node-text.text: A node's `text_hash` field is always the hex digest of `hashlib.sha256(node.text.encode())`, verified independently in tests against directly-computed SHA-256 values.

three-layer-architecture.text: The codebase is a three-layer stack: data model (`__init__.py`), TMS engine (`network.py`), and persistence (`storage.py`), with `api.py` providing functional API and `cli.py` as a thin argparse wrapper.

three-layer-stack-has-clean-boundaries.text: The architecture enforces strict layer separation: pure data model at bottom, context-managed API with dict returns in the middle, and pure-formatter CLI at the top

justifications.label: Each layer's purity constraint (no behavior, load-save atomicity, no business logic) prevents cross-layer coupling

timeout-after-successful-search-preserve.text: If the LLM tool-call search succeeds before a subsequent `invoke_model` timeout, the fallback returns the already-found beliefs rather than `NO_BELIEFS_MSG`.

tms-core-is-crash-safe.text: The TMS core provides crash-free truth maintenance: deterministic termination, pure evaluation, and conservative failure semantics ensure correct results across all reachable nodes.

justifications.label: The engine's correctness guarantees (purity, termination, conservatism) hold only if all dependent references resolve — a dangling entry in `node.dependents` triggers an uncaught KeyError

tms-core-is-crash-safe-v2.text: The TMS's justification evaluation and truth propagation mechanisms support deterministically terminating, side-effect-free computation: uniform validity rules for SL and CP justifications are evaluated as pure functions with no side effects, and propagation is bounded by BFS traversal, stop-on-unchanged checks, and fixpoint iteration.

tms-core-is-deterministic-and-conservati.text: The TMS engine produces deterministic, terminating truth maintenance through uniform pure evaluation, guaranteed convergence, and conservative asymmetric failure semantics for missing nodes.

justifications.label: Three orthogonal engine properties combine into a single correctness guarantee: purity ensures no hidden state, termination ensures completion, and asymmetry ensures safe-by-default behavior

tms-handles-all-conditions-safely.text: The TMS core handles both normal operation (crash-free truth propagation via BFS with stop-on-unchanged) and exceptional conditions (deterministic contradiction resolution via backtracking with least-entrenched selection) through shared propagation infrastructure — no reachable execution state leads to undefined behavior.

justifications.label: Normal and exceptional paths share infrastructure and both terminate correctly

tms-provides-revisability-not-certainty.text: The TMS design provides traceable, revisable reasoning rather than certainty: every belief records its complete justification chain back to premises, beliefs are automatically retracted when support changes, and the epistemological status of each belief is mechanically traceable via `reasons explain`.

token-budgets-are-accurate-bidirectional.text: Token budget management is accurate in both directions: the compact module reliably constrains output size for context-limited consumers, while the derive pipeline correctly allocates input budgets per agent — ensuring resource-bounded operation across the entire LLM integration surface.

justifications.label: Both token budget mechanisms (output-constraining compact and input-allocating derive) are independently accurate, yielding bidirectional budget correctness across the LLM boundary

topic-assignment-uses-exact-token-match.text: `_assign_topics` splits node IDs on `[-._:]` delimiters and assigns a node to the first topic whose label appears as a whole token; partial or substring matches (e.g., topic `"ml"` vs. node `"machine-learning-models"`) never trigger assignment.

topics-cli-exits-zero-on-empty-graph.text: The `reasons topics` CLI command exits with code 0 and prints "No topics found" when the graph contains no nodes; empty data is a valid state, not an error

topics-filters-short-words-and-stopwords.text: Topic extraction excludes tokens with fewer than 3 characters and a curated English stop-word list; both filters apply before frequency counting

topics-result-shape-is-exact.text: `api.topics()` always returns a dict with exactly two top-level keys: `"topics"` (list of `{"topic": str, "count": int}`) and `"total_nodes"` (int); no additional keys are emitted

topics-tokenizer-recognizes-four-delimit.text: The topic tokenizer splits node IDs on exactly four delimiters: hyphen, dot, colon, and underscore; any new delimiter must be added to both the implementation and the corresponding test

topology-accurate-self-correction-is-qua.text: Self-correction achieves quality completeness on accurate convergent topology — every correction is grounded, documented, convergent, evolution-tolerant, and propagates through complete dependency tracking to deterministic stable states.

justifications.label: Quality completeness of self-correction (all dimensions) combined with topological accuracy of all corrections (complete dependency tracking with convergence)

topology-complete-governance-produces-ri.text: Every topology-complete transition within the rich governance framework produces metadata-enriched traceable state — transitions that reach all transitively dependent nodes simultaneously govern richer state than binary truth values, including retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, and supersession metadata.

justifications.label: topology-complete governance and rich state governance converge

topology-complete-governance-produces-ri.text: Topology-complete transitions within the rich governance framework support the complete propagation of metadata-enriched state changes through the dependency graph with deterministic recoverable outcomes. Dialectical revision, as a governing mechanism within this framework, extends state beyond binary truth values, producing traceable deterministic changes to retraction flags, stale reasons, and access tags rather than being limited to binary IN/OUT transitions.

topology-complete-transitions-are-except.text: Every belief state transition is simultaneously topology-complete (reaching all transitively dependent nodes including outlist-connected ones), traceable (producing deterministic structured diffs), exception-safe (handling contradictions and challenges without corruption), and recoverable (providing guided restoration hints for cascade victims).

justifications.label: Topology completeness ensures no node is missed; exception safety ensures failures during propagation don't leave partial state — together they guarantee correct complete outcomes even under adverse conditions

topology-complete-transitions-within-ric.text: Every topology-complete exception-safe state transition operates within a richly-governed revision system extending beyond binary truth — transitions are doubly exception-safe at both the propagation mechanics and governance framework levels.

justifications.label: Topology-complete transitions and rich governance both independently achieve exception safety; combining reveals double-layered safety where neither mechanism depends on the other for fault tolerance

topology-soundness-is-accurate-and-conve.text: All topology-modifying operations are simultaneously accurate (complete dependency tracking ensures dedup survivor selection reflects the true graph structure) and convergent (structural modifications exhaust their effects through complete traversal and reach deterministic stable states) — topology is both correctly measured and correctly maintained.

justifications.label: Complete dependency tracking and structural exhaustiveness jointly ensure topology soundness

total-invariant-preservation-encompasses.text: Total invariant preservation — comprehensive in scope and architecturally grounded — fully encompasses externally-integrated beliefs that achieve integration parity along all quality axes, establishing that the system's invariant regime makes no distinction between internal and external beliefs at any level.

justifications.label: Two independent "totality" claims (preservation scope and integration quality) combine to yield total invariant coverage over all belief origins

total-preservation-is-indefinitely-audit.text: Total invariant preservation — comprehensive in scope and self-sustaining through minimality — is accompanied by indefinite auditability: every invariant-preserving action across all time leaves traceable history without temporal degradation, meaning the system can prove its own correctness at any point.

justifications.label: Depth-13 — combines totality of preservation with indefinite auditability to yield provable correctness: the system doesn't just preserve invariants forever, it can demonstrate it did so

trace-assumptions-raises-keyerror-for-mi.text: `Network.trace_assumptions(node_id)` raises `KeyError` when the node does not exist in the network.

trace-assumptions-returns-only-root-prem.text: `trace_assumptions` performs a transitive walk through justification antecedents and returns only root premise IDs — intermediate derived nodes never appear in the result.

transaction-per-function.text: Every API function opens the database, does its work, and closes — no shared state, no connection pooling, no long-lived sessions; each invocation is fully independent.

transformations-converge-to-documented-e.text: All structural transformations — mode expansion, negation semantics, identity transformation — are evaluation-transparent (producing identical truth regardless of transformation path), and the system autonomously converges to equilibria that generate deterministic traceable artifacts, meaning any sequence of transformations reaches the same documented stable state.

justifications.label: Evaluation transparency guarantees path-independence; documented convergence guarantees the destination is referenceable — together they ensure transformation order is irrelevant and the final state is always identifiable.

transformations-produce-governed-traceab.text: Every structural transformation — mode expansion, negation semantics, identity transformation — is deterministic, traceable, and boundary-safe, and all transformation results flow through comprehensive self-sustaining output governance that normalizes, authorizes, and self-corrects delivery — creating an end-to-end governed pipeline from belief mutation through information delivery.

justifications.label: Connects the mutation-side traceability guarantee with the read-side governance guarantee to form a complete governed pipeline

truncated-hash-is-one-time-migration.text: A 16-char `source_hash` is treated as a legacy format only when it is a strict prefix of the current full SHA-256; a 16-char value that is not a prefix is reported as genuine `content_changed`, making the 16-char case a one-time migration path rather than a permanent dual-format.

truncated-hash-threshold-is-16-chars.text: A stored `source_hash` of exactly 16 characters that is a prefix of the current full SHA-256 hash is classified as `truncated_hash` (legacy format), not `content_changed`.

truncated-hash-upgrade-opt-in.text: Prefix hash upgrade (16-char truncated SHA-256 to full digest) only occurs when `upgrade_hashes=True` is passed to `check_stale`; without it, truncated hashes produce a warning result with `reason="truncated_hash"`.

trust-and-information-boundaries-are-com.text: The system enforces comprehensive boundaries spanning both architecture and information flow: architectural trust boundaries through self-containment and defensive ingestion pipelines ensure no unvalidated data enters the network, while information boundaries through access-tag authorization, token-budget constraints, and bidirectional external surface control ensure no unauthorized or unbounded data leaves it

justifications.label: Architectural trust (depth-4) controls what enters the system, information boundaries (depth-5) control what exits and flows within — the combination means data is governed at every crossing point in both directions, with no uncontrolled path from external source to internal consumer or from internal state to external observer

trust-boundaries-are-self-maintaining.text: Trust boundaries are both structurally enforced (zero external dependencies, defensive ingestion, format-resilient validation) and dynamically maintained through autonomous convergence (every modification reaches a deterministic stable state within trust boundaries) — the system's trust guarantees require no external enforcement mechanism.

justifications.label: Structural trust enforcement reinforced by autonomous convergence — trust boundaries are a fixed point, not a fragile invariant requiring external policing

trust-boundary-is-architecturally-enforc.text: The system's trust boundary is architecturally enforced through complementary internal and external mechanisms: internal self-containment (zero external dependencies, clean three-layer boundaries) eliminates supply-chain and cross-layer attack surfaces, while defensive external containment (layered validation pipelines, namespace isolation, agent kill-switches) prevents untrusted input from corrupting internal state

justifications.label: Self-containment (no supply chain risk) and defensive containment (no ingestion risk) are independently insufficient — combining them establishes that the trust boundary holds against both external dependency attacks and untrusted input attacks simultaneously

trust-enforcement-is-structural-and-oper.text: System trust boundaries are enforced through two complementary mechanisms: structural containment (zero external dependencies, defensive ingestion pipelines, safe three-layer architecture) provides static trust guarantees, while format resilience at all external interfaces (parser fallbacks, schema evolution tolerance, hallucination filtering) provides dynamic trust that adapts to changing external formats without relaxing validation.

justifications.label: Architectural trust enforcement and format-resilient trust enforcement cover static and dynamic threat dimensions respectively

trustworthiness-is-verifiable-through-ob.text: The revision system's complete trustworthiness (verifiable soundness, end-to-end reliability, full auditability) is independently verifiable because the minimality-sustained maintenance loop provides complete observability — every self-correction and maintenance action leaves traceable evidence that can be inspected.

justifications.label: Trustworthiness is claimed; observability makes it verifiable — the combination elevates trust from assertion to auditable property

truth-evaluation-is-transformation-invar.text: Truth evaluation produces identical results regardless of both temporal context (when a justification was attached — at node creation vs. later addition) and structural transformation (premise → justified node via challenge) — all forms of node history and identity change are invisible to the evaluation function, making truth a pure function of current network state.

justifications.label: Context-agnosticism eliminates temporal dependence, while transformation-invisibility eliminates structural dependence — together they establish that truth evaluation is a memoryless function with no path dependence.

truth-is-disjunctive-over-conjunctive-ru.text: A node's truth is a disjunction over justifications (any valid justification makes it IN), where each justification is a conjunction (all antecedents IN and all outlist OUT), and any-mode explicitly reifies OR semantics as per-premise justifications.

justifications.label: These three beliefs collectively define the DNF (disjunctive normal form) evaluation model at the heart of truth computation

truth-semantics-are-emergent-and-uniform.text: Truth maintenance semantics are fully emergent from simple uniform rules: premise behavior arises from empty justification lists, evaluation is pure and type-agnostic across SL/CP, and node truth is a clean disjunction-of-conjunctions — no special cases exist anywhere in the evaluation path.

justifications.label: Three independent design choices (empty-list defaults, uniform eval, DNF truth) converge to eliminate all special-case logic

two-console-entry-points-contract.text: Two console scripts are registered in the distribution: `reasons` → `reasons.cli:main` and `reasons-mcp` → `reasons.mcp_server:main`; both targets must define a callable `main()` or the script will `ImportError`/`ModuleNotFoundError` at first invocation despite successful install.

unified-system-is-a-closed-self-maintain.text: The system forms a closed self-maintaining belief architecture: end-to-end integrity ensures no operation corrupts consistency, while revision completeness ensures any valid belief configuration is reachable — together guaranteeing the system can evolve to any target state while preserving all invariants — only when all known defects and fragilities are resolved.

justifications.label: Combines integrity preservation (no operation breaks consistency) with revision completeness (any valid state is reachable) to characterize the system as algebraically closed; gated by all known defects since this is the strongest possible claim about system correctness

unified-system-maintains-end-to-end-inte.text: The fully unified system — minimal primitives, sound multi-agent scaling, and complete dialectical revision — also maintains end-to-end integrity across all internal and external operations, meaning the design's unification extends from semantic minimality through operational safety to produce a system where every component inherits both the expressiveness and the integrity guarantees of the core.

justifications.label: Pushes to depth-7 by connecting the grand unification (depth-6) with the integrity unification (depth-5); establishes that the system's semantic elegance and operational safety are not separate achievements but a single coherent design property

uniform-semantics-transitively-ground-de.text: Uniform edge-case handling transitively grounds deterministic reliable dialectics through a two-step chain: uniformity reinforces complete negative semantics by ensuring all semantic edge cases (vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents) follow the same rules that produce outlist defeat, and those reinforced semantics in turn ground dialectical challenge/defend with determinism and reliability.

justifications.label: Edge-case uniformity reinforces the negative semantics that ground dialectics — combining reveals a transitive grounding chain from minimality through semantics to dialectics

unknown-type-returns-false.text: Low value — any justification type other than SL/CP returning False is defensive behavior unlikely to affect a developer working in this codebase; the system only creates SL and CP types

untagged-always-visible.text: Nodes with no `access_tags` key in metadata are never filtered by `visible_to` — they are treated as unconditionally public.

untagged-nodes-always-visible.text: Nodes without `access_tags` metadata pass all `visible_to` filters unconditionally and are never hidden by access control.

unused-node-import-in-dangling-test.text: Unstable trivia — an unused import is likely to be cleaned up and is not an architectural invariant.

unused-path-import.text: Dead code observation (`Path` imported but unused) — unstable detail that will change when cleaned up.

update-2026-05-04.text: Status update listing already-tracked beliefs and their blockers; no new architectural claims to extract beyond what is already accepted.

update-node-preserves-justifications.text: `api.update_node` modifies text and source metadata without altering the node's justification list or truth value.

update-proposals-validate-enums-with-saf.text: Invalid `action` values default to `"update"`, invalid `basis` to `"prior-knowledge"`, invalid `failure_mode` to `""` — ensuring every parsed proposal remains actionable even when the LLM hallucinates an enum value.

updated-at-always-refreshed-to-current-t.text: Unlike `created_at`, the `updated_at` metadata field is always set to the current timestamp on every save operation, providing a "last modified" indicator that diverges from `created_at` after the first write.

updated-at-is-iso-8601-with-utc-offset.text: The `updated_at` field is always formatted as ISO-8601 with a `+00:00` UTC offset suffix (e.g., `"2026-11-01T12:00:00+00:00"`), distinguishing it from a naive local timestamp.

upgrade-hashes-mutates-network-in-place.text: When `upgrade_hashes=True`, a stored hash that is a strict prefix of the current file's full SHA-256 is silently upgraded in-place (the node's `source_hash` attribute is mutated to the full hash) and is NOT reported as stale.

user-interface-is-verified-and-fault-tol.text: The complete user-facing stack is both structurally verified (pure delegation with hermetic integration tests ensuring no business logic leaks into the CLI) and operationally resilient (every information flow path is fault-tolerant with graceful degradation and governed output) — users never encounter unverified logic or ungoverned failure modes.

justifications.label: Verified atomic delegation chain (depth-4) combined with fault-tolerant governed information flow (depth-5) establishes the user interface as both correct and resilient

uv-lock-is-untracked-by-policy.text: `uv.lock` is deliberately excluded from version control, meaning dependency resolution is not pinned to a single transitive version set across developer and CI environments, introducing potential non-reproducibility unless compensated by exact version specs in `pyproject.toml`.

validate-proposals-partitions-not-raises.text: `validate_proposals` never raises exceptions — it partitions proposals into `(valid, skipped)` tuples where each skip carries a human-readable reason string

validate-proposals-rejects-jaccard-simil.text: `validate_proposals` skips any proposal whose tokenized ID has >= 0.5 Jaccard similarity to an existing OUT belief, returning "similar to retracted" in the skip reason — preventing re-derivation of retracted beliefs under variant names

verified-correctness-extends-to-all-back.text: Verified production correctness — spanning all belief origins with deterministic state trajectories and full maintenance loop observability for indefinite independent verification — extends identically across both SQLite and PostgreSQL storage backends with no backend-specific safety gaps.

justifications.label: Observable verified correctness (depth-12) should hold across all backends (depth-4), but PgApi's incomplete API coverage means PostgreSQL cannot yet guarantee the same verified correctness as SQLite

verified-correctness-has-indefinitely-au.text: Verified production correctness — observable and permanently documented across all belief origins with deterministic state trajectories — converges to equilibria that are themselves trajectory-documented and indefinitely auditable, creating a self-reinforcing documentation loop where correctness verification and equilibrium auditability share the same permanent evidence base.

justifications.label: Permanently documented correctness (depth-11) and indefinitely auditable equilibria (depth-14) share overlapping audit infrastructure — combining them closes the loop between verifying correctness and documenting convergence

verified-correctness-is-indefinitely-obs.text: Verified production correctness — spanning all belief origins with deterministic state trajectories — is both independently observable through the fully characterized maintenance loop and indefinitely sustainable through minimality's fixed-point self-maintenance, ensuring correctness can be verified at any future point without temporal degradation of either the correctness or the ability to observe it.

justifications.label: Independent observability of verified correctness (depth-10) combined with indefinite loop sustainability (depth-11) ensures correctness verification has no time horizon

verified-correctness-is-independently-ob.text: Production correctness verified across all belief origins is independently observable through the fully characterized maintenance loop — every correctness claim can be audited by inspecting the same deterministic traceable history that the maintenance loop produces, without trusting the system's self-assessment.

justifications.label: Verified correctness (depth-9) combined with full observability (depth-9) eliminates the need for trust — correctness is not asserted but demonstrated through inspectable history

verified-correctness-is-observable-and-p.text: Verified production correctness spanning all belief origins is both independently observable (every correction is visible through the fully characterized maintenance loop without requiring trust in the system's self-reports) and permanently documented (every state change produces comprehensive artifacts that survive persistence boundaries and format evolution) — correctness is not merely achieved but externally auditable with durable evidence.

justifications.label: Observability provides real-time independent verification while permanent documentation provides historical evidence — together they make correctness claims falsifiable by external parties

verified-correctness-is-permanently-docu.text: Verified production correctness spanning all belief origins is backed by a permanent, comprehensive audit trail — the system not only achieves correct state trajectories across all provenance boundaries, but permanently documents every self-correction that maintained that correctness, with no temporal degradation of either the guarantees or their documentation.

justifications.label: Origin-spanning verified correctness + permanent self-correction audit trail means every correctness claim is permanently evidence-backed

verified-interface-controls-bidirectiona.text: All information flowing through the system's verified, fault-tolerant user interface is controlled in both directions: inbound through production-hardened LLM integration with bounded execution and fail-soft semantics, outbound through deterministic authorized access-controlled output — the verified interface serves as a trustworthy gateway that neither admits uncontrolled inputs nor emits unauthorized outputs.

justifications.label: Bidirectional information control + verified fault-tolerant interface means the user-facing surface is a fully controlled gateway

verified-mutation-correctness-across-bou.text: Every mutation source produces fully correct persisted state that preserves boundary-agnostic integrity — not just safe operation, but verified output correctness across internal/external boundaries and all source types — only when implementation-level defects in propagation and budget allocation are resolved.

justifications.label: safe+uniform operation and boundary-agnostic integrity together imply output correctness, but the agent count bug can misallocate LLM budgets and propagation's unchecked dependent access can crash mid-cascade

verified-production-correctness-spans-al.text: Verified production correctness extends universally across all belief origins: the complete architecture achieves verified correctness with deterministic state trajectories and lifecycle-complete monitoring, AND every state change for every belief — including externally-originated ones at full integration parity — follows a deterministic path with complete traceability.

justifications.label: Connecting two orphan depth-8 beliefs — verified correctness is not limited to internal beliefs but extends to all origins because deterministic history covers the full provenance space

verified-revision-completeness-at-all-re.text: The deterministic lifecycle-complete architecture achieves verified uniform revision completeness — every belief case handled uniformly within predictable monitored state trajectories AND every node ID reference crossing a system boundary validated against the actual network — eliminating the possibility of revision operations acting on phantom references.

justifications.label: Uniform revision within deterministic architecture achieves full trust only when all reference boundaries have validated coverage

verify-all-reports-corruption-never-rais.text: `verify_all()` / `api.check_integrity()` always returns a well-formed dict with `text_mutations`, `chain_mutations`, and `missing_hashes` keys — it reports corruption as data rather than raising exceptions, even on cyclic or corrupt graphs.

verify-belief-raises-keyerror-for-unknow.text: `api.verify_belief("nonexistent-id")` raises `KeyError` (not a dict return or silent skip) when the node does not exist in the database

verify-beliefs-never-reads-files.text: `verify_beliefs()` does not call `read_source()` or touch the filesystem; the caller (e.g., `api.py`) must resolve and read source files and pass the content as the second element of each `(belief_dict, source_content_or_None)` tuple.

verify-beliefs-single-llm-call-no-batchi.text: `verify_beliefs()` sends all beliefs in exactly one `invoke_model` call regardless of count; there is no internal batching, chunking, retry, or fallback model — the only safeguard against prompt overflow is the 30,000-character per-source truncation cap.

verify-confirmed-stamps-verified-at.text: A CONFIRMED verdict from the LLM causes `api.verify_belief` to set a non-null `verified_at` timestamp on the node record in the database

verify-dependents-is-pure-observer.text: `verify_dependents` is a read-only auditor that re-derives expected dependents from justifications and diffs against stored values, returning a list of error strings without ever mutating `nodes[*].dependents`.

verify-dependents-is-read-only.text: `Network.verify_dependents()` never modifies the dependents index; it returns a list of human-readable error strings without side effects

verify-dependents-is-readonly.text: `verify_dependents()` never modifies `node.dependents`; it only reads and reports discrepancies as a list of human-readable strings containing `"extra"` or `"missing"`.

verify-dry-run-performs-no-llm-call-and-.text: `dry_run=True` in `api.verify_belief` short-circuits before any LLM invocation and returns an empty `results` dict with `dry_run=True`, making the call fully read-only

verify-llm-call-exceptions-propagate.text: The "no-raise" guarantee in `reasons/verify.py` applies to file-reading and response-parsing paths only; exceptions from `invoke_model` (network timeout, auth error) propagate uncaught to the caller, so `api.py` must handle LLM-call failures.

verify-parse-drops-malformed-entries.text: `parse_verify_response()` silently discards individual JSON entries that lack a string `"verdict"` key (or where `verdict` is not a string) rather than failing the entire batch; only structurally valid entries appear in the returned dict, and verdicts are normalized to uppercase.

verify-read-source-resolves-relative-to-.text: `read_source()` derives the resolution directory from the database file's parent path (`Path(db_path).parent`) and passes it as `db_dir` to `resolve_source_path`, so source paths are resolved relative to the database's location, not the current working directory.

verify-trace-redirects-derived-beliefs-t.text: When `trace=True` and the target node is derived (has an `sl` field), `api.verify_belief` verifies the premise nodes listed in `sl` rather than the derived node itself, and sets `is_derived=True` in the result

version-is-manual.text: The version is statically declared in `pyproject.toml` with no dynamic version plugin, `__version__` import, or SCM-based versioning — it must be bumped manually.

visibility-is-subset-check.text: `_is_visible` requires ALL of a node's `access_tags` to be present in the caller's `visible_to` list (subset check, not intersection); nodes with no tags are always visible.

visible-to-is-optional-filter.text: `_parse_visible_to` returns `None` when `--visible-to` is absent, which the API interprets as "no access restriction"; it never defaults to an empty list.

visible-to-superset-semantics.text: A node with `access_tags: ["finance", "hr"]` is only visible to callers whose `visible_to` list contains both tags (superset/subset check, not intersection).

warning-log-contract-action-target-value.text: Dangling-dependent warnings in `net.log` have `action="warn"`, a `target` field with the ghost node ID, and a `value` string containing both `"dangling"` and the parent node ID.

warning-log-schema-stable.text: Dangling-dependent warnings use the dict schema `{action: "warn", target: <ghost_id>, value: <str containing "dangling" and parent_id>, timestamp: <str>}` and tests enforce all four fields.

what-if-is-read-only-never-persists.text: The `what_if()` MCP tool computes the full retraction/assertion cascade in memory but never writes to the database — subsequent `show_node` calls reflect the original unmodified state.

what-if-operations-mutate-cache-copy.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` operate on a copy of the cached `Network` object, so their hypothetical mutations never corrupt the shared cache; the cached original retains its pre-hypothetical truth values.

what-if-simulations-use-deepcopy.text: The SQLite-path `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, and `what_if_supersede` functions operate on a `copy.deepcopy(net)` and never write to disk, returning predicted truth-value effects without mutating the cached or persisted network.

wiki-llm-failure-silent-fallback-to-dete.text: If LLM page generation fails in `build_wiki` (timeout, model error, bad response), the affected topic group silently falls back to the deterministic per-node markdown rendering; no exception propagates to the caller and the page is still produced.

with-network-is-sole-db-lifecycle-manage.text: Every API function accesses the SQLite database exclusively through `_with_network(db_path, write=False)` — a context manager that loads a Network from Storage, yields it, and saves only on clean exit when `write=True`. No API function manages Storage directly.

with-network-write-atomicity-and-pubsub.text: The `_with_network` context manager in `api.py` saves the network, publishes pubsub events, and updates the in-memory cache only on a successful write-path exit; if an exception occurs, none of these side effects execute and the prior cache entry is preserved.

write-false-prevents-persistence.text: Functions using `_with_network(write=False)` can mutate the in-memory network (as `what_if_retract` does) but changes are never saved to SQLite; write-or-not is declared upfront and never conditional.

zero-result-sentinel-preserved-after-out.text: When the only belief matching a search or lookup query has OUT status, the API returns a sentinel string ("No results found" / "No beliefs found") rather than an empty string or list, preserving a distinguishable empty-result contract for callers.

zero-runtime-dependencies.text: `ftl-reasons` declares `dependencies = []` in pyproject.toml; the entire `reasons_lib` package runs on Python's standard library alone (sqlite3, json, argparse); PostgreSQL support is opt-in via the `pg` extra

zero-runtime-deps.text: `ftl-reasons` has zero runtime dependencies; the entire library runs on Python's stdlib alone (SQLite via `sqlite3`, dataclasses, etc.).
